Bring me evidence, or do not do it." When he said this to me, in truth he overwhelmed me; I could not answer him on that. So I said: "May Allah reward you with good; God willing, I will not differentiate after this." When I prayed for the first time and did not differentiate, the followers glorified Allah with me, saying: "Subhan Allah!" because their custom was that we differentiate. But after two or three times this passed, and they understood that there is no differentiation, and each one began to take a thousand accounts so that he would not go and forget in his prayer and err before the people. It may be that this is supported by the fact that the Prophet did not differentiate between the takbirs: when a pulpit (minbar) was made for him, he (ﷺ) would stand on the pulpit, recite, and bow on the pulpit; when he wanted to prostrate, he came down from the pulpit and prostrated on the ground. Then he (ﷺ) said: "I only did that so that you may follow me and learn my prayer"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari, no. 917, and Muslim, no. 544/44), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]]. As for his saying "so that you may learn my prayer," this is yes, whenever a person is raised and visible to the followers, they learn more. But "so that you may follow me"? This is evidence that he did not differentiate between the takbirs, otherwise following would be by differentiating between the takbirs. And Allah knows best.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: Some people set aside Friday for visiting graves. Is there a basis for this in the Sharia?
* The Shaykh: As for specifying Friday for visiting graves, I do not know of any basis for it in the Sharia. But some jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, said: visiting should be on Friday; and some of them also said: on Friday before sunrise. But since this view has no trace of evidence, it should not be acted upon as a rule; visiting graves is at any time. As I indicated earlier, before the prayer the Prophet (ﷺ) visited the graveyard at night, as in the long hadith of 'A'ishah[[Reported by Muslim, no. 974/103, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]].
* The student: Thank you, may Allah grant you thanks. This one says: We often hear about raising the hands in supplication after voluntary prayer and wiping the face after the supplication. What is the ruling on that, may Allah reward you?
* The Shaykh: As for wiping the face with the hands after supplication, whether after a voluntary prayer or in another place, there are hadiths reported about this, but all of their chains are weak, all of them weak. Some scholars said: the combination of these weak chains raises the hadith to the level of hasan (sound) li-ghayrihi (through another), which the people of hadith call hasan li-ghayrihi, meaning not in itself; and on this Ibn Hajar went, as in Bulugh al-Maram.

Other scholars said: these weak hadiths are not strengthened by the multiplicity of their chains, due to their severe weakness. Among those who held this view was Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said: wiping the face with the hands after supplication is not a Sunnah. Not wiping is more appropriate, because if it were a Sunnah it would be well known and famous. As for raising the hands in supplication, this also has no basis, neither after the obligatory prayer nor after the voluntary prayer. The most that is reported on it is that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which supplication is most heard?" He said: "In the last part of the night and after the prescribed prayers"[[Reported by al-Tirmidhi, no. 3499, and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 9856, from the hadith of Abu Umamah.]]. And the word "adbar": does it mean its end, or what follows it?

Some scholars say: "adbar al-salawat" means what follows them, and others say it means their end. Nevertheless, it is not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he raised his hands in supplication, neither after the obligatory prayer nor after the voluntary prayer. Had it been good, the Prophet (ﷺ) would have explained it to his community, either by his words or by his deeds, or Allah would have facilitated for someone among the Companions in his time to do it, or in his presence, until its legislation is established. But what appears to me preponderant is that if what is tied to "adbar" is remembrance (dhikr), then it is after the prayer; and if what is tied to "adbar" is supplication (du'a'), then it is before the salam. The evidence: remembrance was commanded by Allah after the prayer, He said: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah﴾ [an-Nisa' 103]; and supplication was commanded by the Prophet (ﷺ) before the salam, in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, when he mentioned the tashahhud, he said: "Then let him choose from supplication whatever he wishes"[[Agreed upon (Bukhari, no. 835, and Muslim, no. 402/55), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with the wording: "Then let him choose from supplication what is most pleasing to him and supplicate with it."]].

On this basis we say: what is reported of supplication restricted to "adbar al-salawat" we take to mean before the salam, because that is the place of supplication; and what is reported of remembrance restricted to "adbar al-salawat" we take to mean after the salam, because that is what Allah commanded in His words: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [an-Nisa' 103]; and because the meaning requires that supplication be before the salam, since before a person gives the salam he is still before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When he turns away from his prayer, he turns away. So which is better: to confide in your Lord in supplication while you are confiding in Him in your prayer, or after you have turned away?
* The student: In the prayer is better.
* The Shaykh: In the prayer is better, yes.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: We heard that your eminence has authenticated the completion of the supplication after the adhan: "Innaka la tukhlifu al-mi'ad" [[Reported by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 1933, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]]. Is that correct?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is correct. I authenticated it, and so did others. I do not mean that I authenticated it myself; rather it was authenticated by others among the people of knowledge who are more knowledgeable than us in hadith. Whoever said it is weak was refuted in my presence and could not answer the refutation, because the one who said it is weak was confused by one of the narrators: there is a narrator whose name is shared by two men, one of them weak and the other trustworthy, and the one who weakened it thought the name refers to the weak man, so he weakened it for that reason. Those who authenticated it said: this man you imagined is not the one intended in the context, and therefore this wording is the authentic one.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: A man sold his palm trees to another man, and each of them assumed the other had paid zakat on the fruit; after a year it became clear that neither had paid it. Is the zakat upon the seller or the buyer? And may he give money in place of the fruit?
* The Shaykh: The zakat is upon the seller; that is, if fruits are sold and they are of the kind subject to zakat, the zakat is upon the seller, because the goodness (salah) has appeared in his property, and when the ripening of the fruit appears, zakat becomes due on it. Based on this, our answer to this question is: the seller must pay zakat on it; he pays zakat on the fruit of his palms that he sold. And how does he pay it? He gives out half of its tenth if it is irrigated with buckets (makayil) or with water-wheels (sawani); I think the water-wheels do not exist here.
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Then by buckets: he gives out half the tenth. How much is half of a tenth in relation to a hundred? O calculators, how much is half a tenth in relation to a hundred?
* A student: A quarter of a tenth.
* The Shaykh: No, sir, a quarter of a tenth; five percent. A quarter of a tenth in relation to a hundred is five percent. And if it is irrigated by flowing water or by rain from the (...) or otherwise?
* A student: Its tenth.
* The Shaykh: How much is due? The tenth. How much is a tenth in relation to a hundred?
* A student: Ten.
* The students: Ten percent.
* The Shaykh: Ten percent. So if he sold for ten thousand, and it is of what is irrigated by buckets, how much does he give?
* A student: Five hundred.
* The Shaykh: Five hundred. If he sold for ten thousand, he gives five hundred. If it is rain-fed (ba'l), how much does he give? He gives a thousand, because it is the tenth.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: Is there a specific Sunnah for visiting a specific grave, such as a Muslim visiting the graveyard and visiting the grave of his father or mother with a special visit and supplicating for him?
* The Shaykh: I do not know of a Sunnah from the Messenger (ﷺ) concerning this. But the practice of the Muslims continues, visiting the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his two companions, which is among the specific graves, and they visit their relatives and supplicate for them, which is among the things related to specific graves. As for what the Sunnah is known for, it is visiting graves in general, to remind a person of the Hereafter. How does it remind him of the Hereafter? These people you see now, whose graves you see, were yesterday on the surface of the earth, walking as you walk, eating as you eat, drinking as you drink, dressing as you dress, and enjoying their families as you enjoy yours. And now they have become pledged in their graves by their deeds; no one can add a good deed to his good deeds, nor reduce an evil deed from his evil deeds. Each one of these people did not think he would die except after a long time, but hope deceived him. Will your heart not be reminded by that?

...it may happen. Yesterday they were walking with you, and now they are in their graves. Why do you remember them? So that you may prepare for the day when you will be like them. Today you visit them, and tomorrow people will visit you. So be mindful of this, my brother, and seize the opportunity while you are still alive in the time of respite. Know that it is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that: "When the deceased dies, three things go out with him: his wealth, his family, and his deeds. Two of them return and one remains. His wealth and family return, and his deeds remain."[[Agreed upon hadith: al-Bukhari, no. 6514, and Muslim, no. 2960/5, from Anas ibn Malik, with the wording: "Three things follow the deceased."]] So prepare yourself for that, my brother. Then, along with this, supplicate for these brothers: "Peace be upon you, abode of a believing people, and we, if Allah wills, will join you. May Allah have mercy on those of us who went before and those who come after. We ask Allah for well-being for us and for you. O Allah, do not deprive us of their reward, do not put us to trial after them, and forgive us and them."

* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner asks: Has any part of the Qur'an been revealed without the intermediary of Jibril (peace be upon him)? And what is the position regarding the authentic hadith whose meaning is that Jibril was with the Messenger (ﷺ) when he saw a gate in the heaven open, and an angel descended from it bearing the Umm al-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and the final verses of al-Baqarah?[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, no. 525, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, with the wording: "I was given the Opening of the Book and the final verses of Surat al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne."]]
* The Shaykh: The basic principle is that the one who brought down the Qur'an was Jibril (peace be upon him), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth﴾ [an-Nahl 102], and as He the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 192–195]. So if authentic reports come that some verses were brought down by someone other than Jibril, then these reports specify this general statement. The specification of general statements from the Book and the Sunnah is a valid matter, as whoever investigates it knows. Otherwise, the basic principle is that Jibril (peace be upon him) is the one who brought it down upon the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 97].
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner asks and says: Many young men are lax about shaving the beard, or part of it, and about lengthening their garments. What is your advice to them so that they may give up this violation with which many Muslims are afflicted, may Allah guide them?
* The Shaykh: Praise be to Allah that the questioner did not say "most young men," but said "many young men," and there is a difference between "many" and "most." I agree with him on this. Most young men, praise be to Allah, are committed in their character, in their worship, and also in their customs. Those he referred to among the young men are now, praise be to Allah, a minority. We ask Allah the Exalted to guide them so that they follow the truth, and that is not difficult for Allah. When a person looks at where he goes if he opposes the path of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and what he guided to, where does he go? To the path of "those who have earned anger and those who are astray"?! Subhan Allah! Shaving the beard is the practice of whom? The polytheists and the Magians. Keeping the beard is the guidance of whom? The messengers, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous. "The Prophet (peace be upon him) had a great beard, a thick beard."[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. 684, from Ali ibn Abi Talib.]] It filled from here to here, from his chest. Harun said to his brother Musa: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head﴾ [Ta-Ha 94]. ﴿Do not seize me by my beard﴾. So did he have a beard or not? Yes. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) informed that "the beard is part of the fitrah"[[Narrated by Muslim, no. 261/56, from Aishah, with the wording: "Ten things are part of the fitrah: trimming the mustache, and leaving the beard."]], the natural disposition upon which Allah created creation. So the beard is fitrah. The beard is the way of those upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous. Shaving the beard opposes the way of whom?
* The student: The way of the messengers.
* The Shaykh: Shaving the beard opposes the way of whom? Shaving the beard opposes the way of whom?
* The student: The way of the Jews.
* The Shaykh: The polytheists and the Magians. Shaving the beard is altering the creation of Allah without permission. Shaving the beard is altering the creation of Allah without permission. Is one of these reasons not enough to move the believer to leave his beard, from the one who said: "Oppose the Magians: leave the beards and trim the mustaches"?[[Narrated by Muslim, no. 260/55, from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "Trim the mustaches and let the beards grow; oppose the Magians."]]
* The student: The Messenger (ﷺ).
* The Shaykh: Who said it? The Messenger (peace be upon him). Tell me, by Allah, if Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, were in front of you now saying: "Oppose the polytheists: leave the beard and trim the mustache," could you come out before him with your beard shaved after he told you that, or not?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: As long as you believe in him with complete faith, you cannot do this at all. At least be ashamed before the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds and your imam, whom you hope Allah will gather you with in his company on the Day of Resurrection, saying this to you, and you come out opposing him and disobeying him. Shaving the beard is following a way other than the way of the believers and disobedience to the command of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers—We will leave him in what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination﴾ [an-Nisa' 115]. This verse, although it was revealed concerning complete opposition that leads to disbelief, nevertheless everyone who opposes the Messenger in a matter has a share of what this noble verse deserves. I do not want to apply this verse to the one who shaves his beard. Do not go tomorrow saying: "Ibn Uthaymin says: the one who shaves his beard will burn in Hell." Rather, I say: any person who opposes the Messenger and follows other than the way of the believers has a share of this verse, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic, the most just of judges, recompenses every person according to what he deserves. Moreover, the one who shaves his beard walks among the believers, saying to people: "Bear witness that I am disobedient to the Messenger." I say: the one who shaves his beard walks among people, saying: "Bear witness that I am disobedient to the Messenger." You may say to me: "People constantly pass by me with their beards shaved, and they do not say: 'Bear witness that I am disobedient.'" True, or not? But this is testimony by action. They make me witness against themselves by what?
* The student: By their action.
* The Shaykh: By their action. Correct, they do not say: "I am disobedient," but their action means a testimony that they oppose the Messenger (peace be upon him). Is testimony by action possible or not? Testimony occurs by action and occurs by speech. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah testifies that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾ [al-Munafiqun 1]. Is this speech or action? This is speech. ﴿But Allah testifies to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge﴾ [an-Nisa' 166]. This is also speech. But Allah's support of the Messenger (peace be upon him), and the manifestation of his religion over all religions, is testimony by what? By action. Testimony by action. Allah testified that His Messenger is true and that his religion is the truth, because Allah made it prevail. It is said: testimony by action may be in support, and it may be testimony by action in condemnation and invalidation.

Some historians mentioned that Musaylimah the Liar, who claimed prophethood at the end of the Messenger's life (peace be upon him) and said he was the Messenger of Allah, was approached by some of his followers, who said to him falsely and deceitfully: "O Messenger of Allah, this boy of ours has a head partly shaved, part of it has no hair, and part of it has hair. Wipe over it, perhaps Allah will make the hair of his whole head grow." So he wiped over his head, and the existing hair fell out. This is testimony by what: support or denial? Support that he is a messenger, or denial?
* Student: Denial.
* The Shaykh: Denial. They brought him so that when he wiped his head, the hair that had not grown would appear, but when he wiped his head, what existed fell out.

There is also another story. They say: a man who owned a well came to him and said: "My well's water has decreased." He had heard that when the Messenger (peace be upon him) came at the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, they had said that the well was short of water, so he took water, rinsed his mouth with it, and spat it into the well, and the water rose. This was a sign for the Messenger (peace be upon him), a support. Musaylimah the Liar said to him: "I will come to you." So he came, took water, rinsed his mouth with it, and spat it into the well that had little water. When he spat into the well, the water sank. Was that a honor or a humiliation?
* The student: A humiliation.
* The Shaykh: A humiliation and a denial. This testimony, do we do it by action or by speech?
* The student: By action.
* The Shaykh: Allah testified that he was a liar by what?
* Student: By action.
* The Shaykh: By action, because Allah decreed something that indicates his lie. I say: when the one who shaves his beard passes by us after shaving it, he makes us witness by his action to what? That he is disobedient to the Messenger (peace be upon him). We ask Allah for guidance for us and for them.
* The student: Amin, O Lord.
* The Shaykh: Then what does the one who shaves his beard gain? Will he remain young, or will he remain in old age? Answer, brothers.
* The student: He remains in old age.
* The Shaykh: If a person, when he shaved his beard, returned to youth, then the poet's words would be possible, but they are not:
"Oh, if only youth would return one day, so I could tell it what old age has done."
Is that possible or not possible? It would be possible. Because I said to someone: "Shave your beard and you will become young," and this is not possible. But he gains from it opposing the way of the messengers and agreeing with the way of the polytheists and the Magians. Moreover, my brothers, I am astonished that a people should appear with their religion and customs in what is called the "Khanafis" (a term for a certain style of young men with unusual, wild appearance). Praise be to Allah, the real Khanafis do not exist in the houses now, but these people have appeared among us. A person leaves his head and leaves the sideburns, and by Allah I do not know whether all of it or part of it.
* The student: He does not leave them, it is simple...
* The Shaykh: He does not leave the sideburns and shaves the rest. They have come out of what? Out of the customs of people and out of the Sunnah, and they paid no attention to that, even though they are few. That is, they have a determination greater than the determination of the one who wants the Sunnah in keeping the beard. How can someone have determination in falsehood, by which he has departed from the Sunnah and from customs, while you, O believing young man, do not have determination to agree with the Messenger (peace be upon him)?

But I give you good news, praise be to Allah, that these people have now become few, they have become few, praise be to Allah, because they have come to know where they are heading. So people now are between one who has completely shaved his beard, and one who has shaved most of it leaving only the chin, and between one who adheres to the Sunnah without harm to it, who has heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Leave the beards"[[Agreed upon hadith: al-Bukhari, no. 5893, and Muslim, no. 259/52, from Abdullah ibn Umar.]], and said: "We hear and we obey the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds and the imam of the righteous."
* The student: May Allah reward you. This person requests something from the Shaykh, and we too request it from him, may Allah reward him with good, he says.
* The Shaykh: This is the difference between a request and a demand, my brother. Do you agree with the questioner, or shall we see a new invitation for you?
* The student: He says: Honorable Shaykh, we bear witness before Allah to our love for you, and we hope that you will repeat your visit, and that you give us an appointment from now. We ask Allah for help and success for us and for you.
* The Shaykh: Yes. I say to him: May Allah love me for whose sake He loves me, and may He make me and you among His beloved and friends, and among those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor. In truth, I am delighted to come to this place and to benefit from it and what benefit results from it.
* The student: Frequent attendance is not...
* The Shaykh: But among you, or from you, there is a sensible man, who is a trusted person to me and to you. He has decided for me that I should not come except on the last night of Friday in Sha'ban. He told me: "The last night of Sha'ban is only for the people of Zulfi, do not set an appointment for it." I agreed to that, content and submissive. I hope that this, if Allah wills, will be acceptable to you. Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.
* The student: No, we want two visits before it, Shaykh (...). This is a new request, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: Alright, we will see later.
* The student: This questioner says:
* The Shaykh: May Allah grant us and you a good life.
* The student: It is reported in a hadith that the sun prostrates at the Throne and asks permission.
* The Shaykh: Beneath the Throne.
* The student: He wrote: "It prostrates beneath the Throne and asks permission," knowing that what is observed now is that it does not set on the earth when it sets on one part and rises on another part. This leads us to ask about its eclipse and the eclipse of the moon, what is their cause?
* The Shaykh: As for its circling around the earth, that is—meaning the sun—correct. There is no doubt that it revolves around the earth, and by this night and day occur. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you see the sun when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left﴾ [al-Kahf 17]. These are four verbs: when it rises it inclines, when it sets it passes them. The verbs are attributed to the sun, so it is the doer. On this basis, it is what revolves around the earth, and by that night and day occur. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, I have preferred the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord until it [the sun] disappeared﴾ [Sad 32]. Who is the doer? The sun. So the verb is attributed to it: it is what disappeared, not that we disappear from it; it disappeared from us. These are five verbs. ﴿And the sun runs on to its stationary point﴾ [Ya-Sin 38]. The verb "runs" is attributed to what?
* The student: To the sun.
* The Shaykh: To the sun. These are six verbs. Who said them? The All-Creating, the All-Knowing, who knows whom He created: ﴿Should not He who created know, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?﴾ [al-Mulk 14]. Therefore we must take the apparent meanings of these texts, and not oppose them with any theory, whatever the theory may be, because theories come from human perception, while this is from the Informer, the Creator of humans. So we must take this apparent meaning until it becomes clear to us, as with the sun, that the reality is otherwise. As for merely saying that night and day occur by the earth's rotation, we do not accept it or agree with it, even if all the people of its regions agree upon it, unless there is a tangible proof that would be an excuse for us before Allah on the Day of Resurrection if we oppose the apparent meaning of His speech. As for opposing the apparent meaning of our Lord's words merely for the opinion of people whom we have not touched with our hands, nor seen with our eyes, nor smelled with our noses, nor tasted with our tongues, but only heard with our ears, without any proof, it is not permissible for us to oppose the apparent meaning of Allah's words with such opinions at all. If that is so, then the sun revolves around the earth, and when it sets, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Abu Dharr: "It prostrates beneath the Throne."[[Agreed upon hadith: al-Bukhari, no. 3199, and Muslim, no. 159/250, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.]] But do you think its prostration is like our prostration? If the earth were like our bodies, then its prostration would be like ours. But I mean: if the sun were like our bodies, then its prostration would be like ours. But I think it is not like our bodies. Is this expression correct or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: No, my brother, it is not correct. I said: I think it is not like our bodies. Is this expression correct?
* The student: No.

**Shaykh:** What should I say? I affirm that they are not like our bodies, unless by *zann* (thinking, supposing) you mean *'ilm* (knowledge), as in: ﴿Those who think (*yazunnuna*) that they will meet their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah 46]. In any case, we know with certainty that the sun is not like our bodies, is that clear? So its prostration is not like our prostration. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: ﴿Do you not see that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the animals, and many of mankind, and many deserve the punishment﴾ [al-Hajj 18]. Can you witness the prostration of the camel to Allah? Tell me. You do not witness it, other than (...). Does it prostrate? No. But we do not know its prostration. We must believe that it prostrates, but we do not know its modality. If you say: the intended prostration is the prostration of cosmic decree, which is cosmic submission, we say: this is ruled out by the verse, because Allah says: ﴿and many of mankind﴾. Is cosmic prostration for many of mankind, or for all of mankind? Say it, students: cosmic prostration is for all people; does every person prostrate to Allah or not?

If that is so, then the sun's prostration to Allah, Exalted, when it sets beneath the Throne, is a matter whose modality none knows except Allah.

And what is incumbent upon us regarding this matter? What is incumbent upon us? That we believe, submit, and say: the modality is with the Creator of the heavens and the earth; we do not know it.

**Student:** May Allah reward you. This is a continuation of the question: There is no doubt that the lunar eclipse and the solar eclipse are among the signs of Allah by which He frightens His servants. So how is the statement answered of the one who said: if they are a frightening, how do the servants know of Allah's frightening them before it happens?

**Shaykh:** The knowledge belongs to Allah, Glorified be He. There is no doubt that the lunar eclipse and the solar eclipse occur by the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Is that not so?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** And there is no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ is truthful in what he reported, in his saying: "Indeed Allah frightens His servants with them" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (no. 1048) from Abu Bakrah]. These are two matters that are established without doubt, just as we do not doubt our own existence. We do not doubt this. If that is the case, then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, causes the eclipse by natural causes for a legislative wisdom. The natural causes are well known: the cause of the lunar eclipse is the Earth coming between the sun and the moon. The Earth comes between the sun and the moon and so the moon is eclipsed. For this reason, a lunar eclipse can only happen on the nights of *al-ibdar* (the full moon), that is, the nights of the full moon: meaning the second night, the third night, and the fourth night, right?

**Student:** No.

**Shaykh:** A lunar eclipse cannot happen except on the nights of the full moon: the second, third, and fourth nights of the month. Right or wrong?

**Student:** Wrong.

**Shaykh:** When are the nights of the full moon?

**Student:** The "white days" (*ayyam al-bid*).

**Shaykh:** The thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth. It cannot occur except, most commonly, between the fourteenth and the fifteenth, because the moon is exactly opposite the sun, and the light of the moon, by the permission of Allah, is derived from the light of the sun. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day to give sight﴾ [al-Isra' 12]. Whether what is meant is the day itself and the night itself, or what is meant is the sign of the night and the sign of the day, which are the moon and the sun, the point is that the moon's body is dark and gains its light from where?

**Student:** From the sun.

**Shaykh:** From the sun. So when it is opposite it, and the Earth comes between it and the sun, the eclipse occurs. For this reason, if you observe a lunar eclipse, it can never come from the side facing the sun at all; it comes from below, or from the right, or from the left. This differs from the crescent on the nights of the first, second, and third, whose light comes from the direction of the sun. As for this (the eclipse), if it is total it can come from all directions, but if it is partial, generally, it is not from the side facing the sun. In any case, this is known.

From where does the solar eclipse come? Its natural cause is that the moon comes between the sun and the Earth. For this reason, the sun can only be eclipsed on the nights of *al-istisrar* (the nights when the moon is hidden), meaning on day eighteen, nineteen, or twenty, right?

**Student:** Wrong.

**Shaykh:** Wrong. The nights of *al-istisrar* are the nights in which the moon disappears: the twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth, and thirtieth. So if someone tells you the sun was eclipsed on the twentieth, say to him: this is impossible; it can only happen on the twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth, or thirtieth. For this reason, those historians who said that the death of Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet ﷺ, was on the tenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, their statement is wrong without doubt, one hundred percent. The death of Ibrahim was on the twenty-ninth of Shawwal in the tenth year after the Hijrah. The twenty-ninth is among the nights of *al-istisrar*, isn't it?

**Students:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Among the nights of *al-istisrar*, because the moon, by the permission of Allah, comes between the sun and the Earth. Which is higher, the moon or the sun?

**Students:** The sun.

**Shaykh:** Are you certain? Yes, the sun is higher. So when the moon comes at the end of the month, it covers the sun. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills an eclipse, the moon comes, for example, if we assume this is the Earth, the moon comes like this, between the sun and the Earth, and blocks the light of the sun. Who can make the Earth be in an orbit, or in a place, to be precise, in a place that comes between the light of the sun and the moon? Who can do that?

No one can. And likewise the reverse. So the eclipse is a sign of Allah, meaning a sign of His power, Mighty and Majestic. As for it being a frightening, that is evident: the difference in the courses of the sun and the moon, until this occurs, is undoubtedly a frightening and a warning, and it is not in itself a punishment. It is not a punishment in itself, but it is a warning of a punishment whose causes have been established. For this reason, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to turn in fear to the remembrance of Allah, to His supplication, His seeking of forgiveness, prayer, charity, and freeing of slaves. All of this he commanded, and these matters are means of repelling affliction. So if we do that, the affliction whose causes have been established is averted, and the eclipse becomes a sign of what? Of this affliction and this punishment. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when His servants return to Him and turn to Him in fear, He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, and He removes affliction and punishment from them. For this reason, I lean toward the view that the eclipse prayer is obligatory, and that it is not among the recommended acts but among the obligatory ones. Because the Messenger ﷺ went out in fear, to the extent that he was caught up with his cloak. He left his cloak behind, peace be upon him, and went out only with his lower garment from the intensity of his fear, until he was caught up with his cloak and put it on, or had it put on him, until he began dragging it, ﷺ, in fear. And in this great situation, Paradise and Hellfire were displayed to him, until he advanced toward Paradise to take a cluster of its grapes. He said: "If I had taken it, it would have remained among you as long as the world lasts." [A hadith agreed upon: al-Bukhari (no. 5197) and Muslim (no. 907/17) from Abdullah ibn Abbas, with the wording: "And if I had taken it, you would have eaten from it as long as the world remained."] This is the hadith or its meaning. And he held back, because Hellfire was displayed to him and he feared its scorching. He saw in the Fire a woman being punished because of a cat (*hirrah*) she had confined. A *hirrah*, meaning? What is a *hirrah*?

**Student:** A cat (*qitta*).

**Shaykh:** What is a *hirrah*, brothers?

**Student:** The cat.

**Shaykh:** The cat. And what is a cat? The same answer. People say a linguistic point: they say "bis" (to call a cat). The dictionary (al-Qamus) says: the correct form is "bas," and the common people pronounce it with a kasrah. That is the statement of the Qamus. The common people say "bis," but the correct form in the Arabic language is "bas." But do not think of it as a cup of tea being poured; you say "bas."

Now we say: the Messenger ﷺ saw the woman who was punished because of this cat, and he saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire. This man, may Allah protect us, was the first to introduce polytheism among the Arabs and the first to release the *sawa'ib* (free-roaming camels). And he saw the owner of the *mihjan* (a crooked staff) who stole from pilgrims with his *mihjan*. This was a thief who had a *mihjan*, meaning a staff with a bent head. When the pilgrims passed by, he would insert it and drag their goods away. If the pilgrim noticed it, he would say: "By Allah, this *mihjan* has afflicted me, I don't know what to do with it." In any case, he says: "This *mihjan* is what dragged my goods away against my will." And if the pilgrim did not notice it, what would he do?

**Student:** He took it.

**Shaykh:** He took the goods and left. The Prophet, peace be upon him, saw him being punished in the Fire for taking the belongings of pilgrims. This indicates the greatness of the eclipse prayer. For this reason, when the Prophet, peace be upon him, finished, he delivered a great sermon and said, among what he said: "By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." [Narrated by al-Bukhari (no. 6485) from Abu Hurayrah.] He commanded turning to it in fear. For this reason, this prayer is an unfamiliar and unaccustomed prayer, because the cause of it is unfamiliar and unaccustomed. So it is wise that the worship for it should also be unaccustomed. Is there a prayer like the eclipse prayer among the prayers? No. And is there a concealment of the sun from us like its concealment in an eclipse? No. The sun simply sets at the horizon, and likewise the moon.

How is the eclipse prayer performed? The person says the takbir and recites al-Fatihah and a long surah, very long, about the length of Surat al-Baqarah. Then he bows, a very long bowing. Then he rises and recites al-Fatihah and a long surah, long but less than the first. Then he bows and prolongs the bowing, but less than the first. Then he rises and supplicates with what he supplicated during the bowing, roughly the length of his bowing. Then he prostrates and prolongs the prostration roughly the length of his bowing. Then he sits between the two prostrations for about the length of his prostration. Then he prostrates a long prostration. Then he stands for the second rak'ah and does in it as in the first rak'ah, but less in everything that is done. And when he finishes, he delivers an eloquent sermon to the people, admonishing and reminding them, as the Prophet ﷺ did.

Does he recite aloud in it, or silently? Did you not pray the eclipse prayer?

**Students:** Aloud.

**Shaykh:** Aloud. At night or during the day?

**Students:** At night and during the day.

**Shaykh:** At night and during the day. Even if it is a solar eclipse, he recites aloud. Why?

Because the people are gathered, and every prayer in which the whole population of the town gathers together is legislated to be recited aloud. Have you seen the Friday prayer? It is recited aloud. The Eid prayer is recited aloud. The prayer for rain (*istisqa'*) is recited aloud. The eclipse prayer is recited aloud, because it is better that the people pray together in the congregational mosques, not in every mosque. The Sunnah, as the scholars have said, is that the eclipse prayer be performed in the congregational mosques, because the gathering of people humbly beseeching Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and supplicating to Him, is more effective. For this reason, the greatest gathering and the most worthy of being answered is the gathering of people on the Day of 'Arafah, because they are most numerous as a gathering. So the gathering of people in worship and supplication to Him has a standing with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But some people now, and since long ago, perform the eclipse prayer each in his own mosque, because they claim that if they prayed in the congregational mosques, people would be late and no one would go to the mosque. But how wonderful it would be if the people did this recommended act and dedicated their prayer to the congregational mosques, and the people went out in great numbers with humility and saying "Amin" aloud. There is also no harm in women attending the eclipse prayer, as women attended in the time of the Prophet ﷺ.

**Student:** May Allah thank you. This person says: If you would be so kind, O eminent Shaykh, and give us an outline of your scholarly and practical life, may Allah reward you with good?

**Shaykh:** I say to the questioner: if the questioner would kindly excuse me from answering this question, may Allah reward him with good.

**Student:** May Allah bless you. This questioner says: Eminent Shaykh, there is someone who says: the difference between congregational prayer (*salat al-jama'ah*) and individual prayer is a superiority of twenty-seven or twenty-five degrees, and I do not want this difference, and I perform it in my home. What is the ruling on such a person?

And another says: congregational prayer is not obligatory as an individual obligation (*fard 'ayn*), based on the evidence of the two men who came to the Messenger ﷺ at Mina while the prayer had not been established. He said: "Why did you not pray?" They said: "We prayed in our camping places." He did not reprimand them or command them to repeat it in congregation. And a teacher at the university cited this hadith in front of his students, as the questioner says.

**Shaykh:** My answer to this question, first: I direct my advice to this brother who said: "I do not want this virtue." Does he not leave it? Is this man independent of the mercy of Allah? By Allah, a day will certainly come upon him when he will wish that there was in his good deeds one single good deed, not twenty-seven, just one good deed. Let him fear Allah regarding himself, repent to Allah, the Exalted, from his sin, and rejoice in the blessing of Allah upon him through the abundance of reward in congregational prayer. As for this teacher, I believe that if it were said to him: "We will place you at a school where your salary now is three thousand, and we will give you at the second school five thousand, but it is a kilometer further than this one," would he walk or not?

**Student:** He would walk.

**Shaykh:** He would walk, even on his eyelids, not on his feet. He would not say: "I do not want this virtue." Although Allah, the Exalted, says in His Book: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life﴾ [al-A'la 16], and after it: ﴿while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [al-A'la 17]. How can an intelligent person choose the virtue of this world, though it is transient, over the virtue of the Hereafter? The man who gained the virtue, or the virtue itself, and does not choose the virtue of the Hereafter? By Allah, this is foolishness. And this statement truly wounds the feelings. Although recommended matters are optional for a person, praise be to Allah; they are not obligatory. But for him to say so frankly: "I do not want this virtue!!" This is a great thing! It is something a person should fear to say! So I ask this brother teacher to fear Allah regarding himself and regarding his students, and not to let the matter go so far as to belittle the virtues of deeds to the point of saying: "I do not want the virtue." Who would dare to say: "I do not want the reward of Allah nor the virtue of Allah?" This is serious, brothers! I hope that what I am saying now reaches him.

As for it not being an individual obligation, and the use of the hadith of the two men: these two men prayed in their camping places, and that is a particular case. Perhaps these two men did not know that congregational prayer is obligatory, and this is possible. For this reason, they were ignorant that they should pray with the Messenger, peace be upon him, and it is prescribed that when you come to a congregation, you pray with them. And perhaps these two men thought that the Prophet ﷺ had prayed with his companions and it was over. So the matter is a particular case, not a statement with general application, so that we can apply its generality. And as long as there is a possibility, the scholars say: when a possibility arises, the inference is invalidated. So there is no evidence in it at all.

At this point there remains the claim of some people: "If it is more virtuous, then 'more virtuous' (*ism tafdil*, the comparative form) means it is not obligatory, because superiority is not said of an obligatory act." We say to these brothers: may Allah bless you, and grant us and you correct understanding. Your statement that goodness or superiority cannot apply to an obligatory act is wrong. Goodness may apply even to the most obligatory of obligations. Listen to the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [You should] believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives﴾ [al-Saff 10–11]. I will pause so you may complete it: ﴿That is better for you﴾ [al-Saff 11]. What does the reference in the verse point to? Belief in Allah and belief in the Messenger, and striving in the cause of Allah with wealth and lives.

Are belief in Allah and the Messenger among the obligatory matters or among the recommended matters?

**Students:** Among the obligatory matters.

**Shaykh:** The most obligatory of obligations. This is in creed. Take, in actions: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade﴾. Complete it. ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 9].

Can this brother say that the Friday prayer is not obligatory, because Allah said: ﴿That is better for you﴾, and "better" is a comparative form? Or can he not say it?

Can he say that faith is better than disbelief, being in the comparative sense and not in the sense of obligation? The answer?

**Student:** He cannot.

The Shaykh: He cannot. So preferring one act over another does not show that the preferred act is not obligatory. As for the obligation of congregational prayer (salat al-jama'a), its evidence from the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the practice of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) is well known. Listen to the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let one group of them stand with you and let them take their arms. Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come forward and pray with you, taking their precaution and their arms﴾ [An-Nisa' 102]. The command to pray here, in a state of safety, stability and tranquility, is correct? The command here is in what state, what?

The students: Fear.

The Shaykh: In a state of fear and war. Does Allah obligate His servants to perform this prayer, which involves altering the prayer? For the prayer of fear, as you know, involves altering the prayer and departing from some of its pillars or obligations. Would Allah waive these obligations and pillars for the sake of a recommended matter? And would Allah oblige His servants to do something recommended during jihad?

No. And in His words: ﴿Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come forward﴾ [An-Nisa' 102], there is a refutation of the view of those who say that congregational prayer is a communal obligation (fard kifayah), because if it were a communal obligation, the first group would have sufficed. Therefore it is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn). Listen to the Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever hears the call and does not respond, there is no prayer for him, except for an excuse." [Abu Dawud no. 551, Ibn Majah no. 793, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih no. 2064, from Ibn 'Abbas; the wording is Ibn Hibban's.] A man asked his permission to abandon congregational prayer, and he said: "Do you hear the call?" He said: Yes. He said: "Then respond." [Muslim no. 653/255, from Abu Hurayrah.] And the man was blind. He also said, as is authentically related from him: "I have certainly intended to order that the prayer be established, then order a man to lead the people in prayer, then I would go out with bundles of firewood to people who do not attend the prayer, and burn their houses over them with fire." [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari no. 2420 and Muslim no. 651/251, from Abu Hurayrah.] The one who says this, while he is kind and merciful to the believers, is it possible (...) that a person may do it if he wishes, and abandon it if he wishes? No. But you may say: the Messenger said, "I intended," and did not do it; intention is one thing and action is another. We say: Very well, did the Messenger, upon him be prayer and peace, say it as a warning, or did he say it only to encourage prayer, and whoever does not pray, he does not intend to burn him? There is no doubt that he said it as a warning, since such a statement cannot be made about a matter left to one's choice.

As for the Companions, listen to the words of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), as is authentically related from him in Muslim: "I have seen us, and none would stay away from it except a hypocrite, and a man would be brought, supported between two men, until he was placed in the row." [Muslim no. 654/257, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.] Whose practice is this?

The students: The Companions.

The Shaykh: The Companions. The Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the practice of the Companions. Such neglect of congregational prayer, or disparagement of the reward of the Hereafter, is what has made us fall behind, while the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ advanced and, through their religion, came to possess the eastern and western parts of the earth. I hope to Allah, glorified and exalted, that He pardons this teacher for what he did and what he taught his children. I direct my hope to him that he returns again and becomes a scholar devoted to his Lord, an educator before being a teacher, because leading the nation is not by knowledge alone, but by knowledge and what, after that? And by upbringing.

The Messenger ﷺ raised those people by his character, by his deeds, and by his sound guidance. He never commanded anything without being the first to do it, and never forbade anything without being the furthest of people from it. Likewise, scholars must do, if they wish to truly be the heirs of the prophets: they should educate people with what Allah has taught them, so that they may be among the guides who are guided. I think the night has passed.

The student: Dear brothers in Allah, at the close of this lecture, we can only extend our thanks to His Eminence the Shaykh for undertaking the journey to benefit us with these good guidelines. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to place that in the scales of his deeds on the day he meets Him. We also ask him, may Allah reward him with good, not to make his visit long, but to visit us from time to time, so that the visits are not few.

The Shaykh: No, God willing, we will return to them, God willing. We are keen on what is good, God willing.

The student: And we want each one of you to be a means of communication in such gatherings, may Allah reward you with good, calling on his brothers and loved ones. May Allah grant success to all for what is good.

The Shaykh: We thank you all for this blessed meeting, and we ask Allah, may He be exalted, to make it beneficial for us and for you. I add my voice to the brother's call for eagerness to attend the lectures, because at the least of what they are, they are gatherings of remembrance (dhikr), and gatherings of remembrance are the gardens of Paradise. "When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, then graze in them." [At-Tirmidhi no. 3509, from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording "you pass by".] They are all good and all blessing; a person benefits or gives benefit. A person may ask a question whose answer he knows, but people need it, so he becomes the teacher. That is, if you ask the lecturer a question that you know, so that people may know it, you have become the teacher, you are the teacher. And what is the evidence?

The evidence is the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): "When Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about Islam, faith, excellence (ihsan), the Hour, and its signs, he said: 'O 'Umar, do you know who the questioner is?' He said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: 'It is Jibril, who came to you to teach you your religion.' " [Muslim no. 8/1.] Who was answering?

The Messenger ﷺ was answering, and the questioner was Jibril. The Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace, made him a teacher because he was the cause of the teaching; otherwise the direct teacher was the Messenger of Allah, upon him be prayer and peace. But since this was the cause, the motivating reason, the Prophet ﷺ made him a teacher. From here the scholars derived a principle useful in the chapter on retaliation and offences. They said: the one who causes an act is liable just like the direct perpetrator, but with conditions. That is, liability arises through direct action and it arises through causation; so the one who causes is an actor. But in any case, if a causer and a direct perpetrator combine in a matter of offences, the direct perpetrator is given precedence if it is possible to assign liability to him under the known conditions. I will not extend by mentioning them.

But I repeat my hope for your attendance, brothers, especially the young among you and the elderly. The elders who attend here are youths of resolve; their resolve is the resolve of a young man, and old age does not harm one who benefits. And the youth who are heading toward good, we hope for them good, God willing, and for all. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 1, verse 1–7 (part 1 of 9):

All praise is due to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, and turn to Him in repentance. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from the consequences of our deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. Allah, the Exalted, sent him with guidance and the religion of truth, that He might make it prevail over all religion. He conveyed the message, fulfilled the trust, advised the Ummah, and strove in the way of Allah with the striving He deserves until certainty came to him. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and upon his family, his Companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice. He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment.﴾ [al-Ahzab 70–71].

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, Allah is ever, over you, an Watcher.﴾ [an-Nisa' 1].

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice. He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment.﴾ [al-Ahzab 70–71].

To proceed: brothers, you have honored us by participating with you in an evening such as this, for the sake of meeting with you. We praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He has placed in this country, and in other lands of this kingdom, and indeed in other lands of Islam, in this recent era, an Islamic awakening among the youth. The youth are the men of the future. This awakening, praise be to Allah, has a direction and a goal, which we do not doubt is the attainment of implementing the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), an implementation manifested in the belief of the hearts, the statements of the tongues, and the deeds of the limbs. This is the noble goal by which this Ummah prevailed over all the nations of the world in its early generations. It is the goal for which Allah sent the Messengers and revealed the Books. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Mankind was one community, and Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed.﴾ [al-Baqarah 213]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explained in two verses of the Quran that Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it﴾ [at-Tawbah 33]. Do you know what guidance is? And what is the religion of truth?

Indeed, guidance is beneficial knowledge, because by beneficial knowledge a person is guided through the darkness of ignorance. As for the religion of truth, it is righteous action: righteous action that is in accordance with the pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is because the word "religion" (din) is applied to action and is also applied to the recompense for action. In the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3], "religion" here means the action a person performs in order to be recompensed for it. As for "religion" in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [al-Fatihah 4], and in His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what the Day of Recompense is? Then what can make you know what the Day of Recompense is? The Day when no soul will have power for any soul at all, and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Infitar 17–19], "religion" in these verses means the recompense for deeds. Among the well-known sayings is: "As you do, so shall it be done to you," [[Narrated by Ma'mar in al-Jami' (20262), from the hadith of Abu Qilabah, raised (to the Prophet), may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Brothers, I praise Allah and thank Him that He has placed in our country and in the lands of Muslims generally that youthful awakening whose goal is the implementation of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) in belief, in speech, and in action. Scholars must, in the face of that resolve among those youth, be leaders for them, guiding them to the truth, to the straight path, and to following wisdom. Wisdom is knowledge and correctness, and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good.

Knowledge alone, without action, is of no benefit. And knowledge alone, without wisdom, may lead a person to exceed its limits, either by falling short or by going too far.

Brothers, among the blessings of Allah upon us in this land is that Allah has made it easy for us to reach whatever we want in any part of this land, due to the ease of transportation, praise be to Allah. Therefore it is fitting, indeed obligatory, for people of knowledge to always be with these youth, so that the wisdom of the elders and the energy, strength, and determination of the youth may come together in their journey. This gathering, which I do not consider a lecture but call a "meeting" so that it is not attributed to me or to you, is a meeting in which I want to speak about a general matter. I had nothing particular in mind, except that I wanted to speak now about these prayers that we perform every day, obligatory and voluntary, in the mosques and in the homes. I do not wish to discuss their ruling, for the ruling on them is clear. They are one of the great pillars of Islam, indeed the only practical pillar whose abandoner becomes a disbeliever in Allah, a disbelief that expels one from the religion. This is because the pillars of Islam are the testimony that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, paying zakah, fasting Ramadan, and performing Hajj to the House. Concerning the last three pillars (paying zakah, fasting Ramadan, and Hajj), the scholars—may Allah have mercy on them—differed regarding the ruling on one who abandons them not by denying their obligation but out of negligence. The preponderant view, however, is that one who abandons them does not become a disbeliever. As for the prayer, the evidences from the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), and the reported consensus of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, indicate that one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever in a manner that expels him from the religion, even if he acknowledges its obligation. But I want to speak about this prayer: what is said in it, what is done in it, what its purpose is, how it was a connection between the person and his Lord, and why the Lawgiver (ash-Shari') gave it this great care.

That is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, enjoined upon Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this prayer, from Allah to His Messenger (ﷺ) without an intermediary. Where did He enjoin it upon him? Did He enjoin it upon him while Muhammad was on the earth?

No. He enjoined it upon him while Muhammad (ﷺ) was above the seven heavens. And at what time did He enjoin it upon him?

He enjoined it upon him on the most excellent night that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ever had, which is the night of the Mi'raj (Ascension). And how many prayers did He enjoin? What number did Allah prescribe for His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ)? He enjoined upon him that he pray fifty prayers in a day and night. From these three matters—the nobility of the place, the nobility of the time, and the abundance of the number—we derive the importance of the prayer and Allah's love for it. But among the blessings of Allah upon this Ummah is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) descended from the presence of Allah and met Musa ibn 'Imran, peace be upon him, while he was in the sixth heaven, Musa said to him: "What has Allah enjoined upon you and upon your Ummah?" He said: "He enjoined upon me fifty prayers in a day and night." Musa said to him: "Indeed your Ummah cannot bear that, for I have tested the Children of Israel and dealt with them with the utmost effort. So return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening." So the Prophet (ﷺ) kept returning to his Lord until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made them five in practice and fifty in reward. [[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (3207) and Muslim (164/264), from the hadith of Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. This is not from the principle of the reward of a good deed being multiplied tenfold, since every righteous deed is multiplied tenfold. Rather, these five are as though we had prayed fifty prayers, and each prayer has ten good deeds. Multiply fifty by ten: how much does it come to? Fifty times ten is how many? Five hundred good deeds for these five prayers. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills.

So we must know what the wisdom is in Allah's care for this prayer. Consider that these five prayers are fixed to times determined by the sun's movement across the horizon. When the sun begins to rise over the earth, the Fajr prayer is performed, because this is a great and significant change in the horizon, not a trivial one. Who among the creatures can bring this sun to illuminate the world? No one.

﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not listen?﴾ [al-Qasas 71]. There is no deity but Allah. No one brings light except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then comes the time of the sun's decline (zawal), which is its movement from the eastern side to the western side of the horizon. Who can move this great sun from the east of the sky to its west? Tell me, by Allah, who? Say: "There is no deity but Allah."

* Students: There is no deity but Allah.

* Shaykh: No one can move this sun from the east of the sky to its west except its Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, the Lord of the worlds, who says to a thing, "Be," and it is. At this transition from the east of the sky to its west, the Dhuhr prayer is performed. Then comes the 'Asr prayer, until the sun turns yellow and nears sunset, and the necessity of the sunset. Then after the sun sets, the atmosphere changes. How magnificent the earth is if you witness it while you are in an airplane and the sun has set over the earth! By Allah, you will understand the wisdom in His saying: ﴿and by the night when it covers it﴾ [ash-Shams 4], meaning when it covers it over.

Once I left the airport in Qassim a few minutes before sunset. The plane took off, and the sun set for the people of the earth, but we in the sky were still seeing the sun. Glory be to Allah, the night on the earth was like a black garment with which the earth had been covered. Glory be to Allah, the Mighty! This makes clear to you the greatness of His saying: ﴿and by the night when it covers it﴾. At this great transition Allah enjoined upon us a prayer, the Maghrib prayer. Then at the disappearance of the twilight (ash-shafaq) there is also a change. The red twilight is the remnant of the sun's rays. The 'Isha' prayer is performed until when? Until midnight. After midnight the time for 'Isha' ends, and no time remains for the obligatory prayers. But it is a time for voluntary prayer, as the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, and as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The most excellent prayer is the prayer of Dawud: he would sleep half the night, stand in prayer a third of it, and sleep a sixth of it." [[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (1131) and Muslim (1159/189), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]].

At midnight there is no time for the obligatory prayer, but it is a time for voluntary prayer. Then the cycle continues until the time of Fajr arrives at the change of the horizon and its preparation to receive the sun. Thus we understand the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in enjoining the prayer at these times. Furthermore, brothers, the prayer is preceded by purification: purification of the heart and purification of the body. How is the purification of the body achieved? By what? By wudu' (ablution) from the minor ritual impurity (hadath asghar) and ghusl (full bathing) from the major ritual impurity (hadath akbar), and purification of the body from impurities, purification of garments, and purification of the place. All of this is to honor its status. So what is the purification of the heart or the inner purification that precedes this prayer?

First: physical purification. Listen to it in the saying of Allah, when He mentioned the verses of wudu', ghusl, and tayammum (dry ablution). He said: ﴿Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "None of you performs wudu' and perfects the wudu', then says: 'I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves,' except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, to enter through whichever he wishes." [[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (55), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

What kind of purification is this, through the two great testimonies? It is purification of the heart, is it not? Yes, it is purification of the heart. Thus physical purification and purification of the heart are brought together at the beginning of these prayers, so that a person enters his prayer and stands before his Lord with a pure heart, a pure body, and a pure place. What does this care indicate? It indicates the importance of this prayer. Then, when one turns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and stands before Him, you say: "Allahu Akbar" (Allah is greater). He is greater than everything in majesty and grandeur, the Exalted. No one is greater than Allah, the Exalted, in majesty and grandeur. He is greater than everything. Glory be to Allah, the Mighty! How great is the wisdom of Allah! Why was takbir chosen here over tasbih? Because takbir indicates loftiness of status and elevation. For this reason it was the guidance of the Messenger (ﷺ) and his Companions that when they ascended a high place while traveling, they would say "Allahu Akbar." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2994), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, whose wording is: "When we ascended we would say takbir, and when we descended we would say tasbih."]]. I do not know: when you board an airplane and it lifts you from the ground, do you say takbir? A question for whoever has boarded an airplane: when you board the airplane and it takes off and rises from the earth, do you say takbir?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: In any case, whoever has not said takbir should know that this is a place for takbir, because you have risen. And when they descend into a valley, what do they do? They say tasbih. When you descend and go down, you say: "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to Allah). Because when a person rises, he may become self-important and think himself exalted, so he says "Allahu Akbar" to restrain his arrogance and pride. But when he descends and goes down, he says "Subhan Allah," meaning glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, above descent. Descent is a characteristic of the human being, indeed of created beings in general, but loftiness belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So you say "Subhan Allah" at descent, glorifying Allah above the lowliness you are in now.

I say: choosing takbir at the beginning of the prayer is entirely appropriate to this wisdom. Then one begins the prayer (istiftah). Abu Hurayrah asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Hurayrah was among the people most eager for knowledge. He said to the Prophet (ﷺ) one day: "Who among people will be happiest with your intercession, O Messenger of Allah?" Look at what he asked and why: so that he would know who is the happiest of people, to have it firmly in his mind, or so that he would act upon what the Messenger guided him to? Both at once: so that he would know who is happiest with his intercession and would act accordingly. He said: "I thought that none would ask me about this except you, O Abu Hurayrah, because of what I see of your eagerness for knowledge. The happiest of people with my intercession is the one who says, 'There is no deity but Allah,' sincerely from his heart." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (99).]].

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) saw the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say the takbir for the prayer and then fall silent. So he said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me, what do you say during your silence between the takbir and the recitation?" He said: "I say: O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the East and the West. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail." [Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari (744) and Muslim (598/147).]

Do you begin with this?

The question is for everyone: do you begin with this?

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Most people do not begin except with his saying: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk" [Related by Muslim (399/52)]. It is an excellent opening, but we must know the Sunnah so that we can act upon both Sunnahs. "O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the East and the West. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail." I will repeat it for the third time so that I can see who among you has memorised it.

"O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the East and the West. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail." I have said it three times. Which of you will repeat it back to me? Come forward, so that the people can hear.

* A student: "O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the East and the West. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of filth. O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail."

* The Shaykh: Well done. Now, "put distance between me and my sins": this is before one actually commits the sins. Make them far from me so that I do not commit them afterwards. "Cleanse me of them as a white garment is cleansed of filth": make me pure of them. Why did the Prophet ﷺ choose the white garment? Why? Because the slightest dirt shows on a white garment, whereas on a black or red one the trace of dirt does not show unless it is very heavy filth. "O Allah, wash me of my sins with water, snow and hail." You might say: hot water cleans better, correct or not? Does hot water clean better or not? When we wash a garment with soap, do we use cold water, ice, or do we heat the water and wash with it?

* A student: Heating.

* The Shaykh: Heating. So why did he say: "with water, snow and hail"? The scholars said: because he says "wash me of my sins", and these are not material filths, and the punishment for sins is the Fire. So it is fitting that what removes these sins should be hot or cold?

* The students: Cold.

* The Shaykh: Cold. Cold, and this is the wisdom.

If you wish, you may say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk." This is authentic. The first, the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, is stronger in its chain than this one. But this one is what 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to begin with aloud, to teach the people. So shall I combine the two?

No. If you combine them you oppose the Sunnah. Rather, say this at one time and that at another time, sometimes this and sometimes that, so that you act upon both Sunnahs. After this, after the opening (and we know the meaning of the opening), comes "Wajjahtu wajhiya" [Related by Muslim (771/201)]. This is mostly in the night prayer. Now we know the meaning of the opening: the Prophet ﷺ recited it before reciting al-Fatihah, between the takbir and the recitation.

Next, at the takbir: what do we do with the action? Is there an action that accompanies the takbir or not? Is there an action that accompanies the takbir or not?

The answer: yes, there is an action that accompanies the takbir. What is it? That you raise your hands with the fingers joined and extended, like this, up to the level of your shoulders or to the level of the tips of your ears, like this, but do not wipe your ears with them. Some people we see raise their hands and say such-and-such; this has no basis. Raise them like this and say the takbir. Some hadiths indicate that the beginning of the raising coincides with the beginning of the takbir, others indicate that the takbir comes after the raising, and others indicate the raising after the takbir. The matter here is broad. But what is the wisdom behind raising the hands in this way?

The scholars said: it is a sign of exalting the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and of removing the veil between you and Him, so that you feel that you are standing before Him, conversing with your Lord as one who addresses another. Listen to what has been established in the hadith from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves" [Related by Muslim (395/38)]. "I have divided the prayer": what is the prayer? The whole prayer. The prayer here is al-Fatihah, and Allah called it "prayer" because the prayer is not valid without it. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn﴾ [al-Isra 78], meaning: and establish the recitation of dawn. The wisdom in His saying in the four prayers ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, and in the dawn prayer ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾, is that the recitation of dawn is witnessed: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾; and also because the recitation is lengthened in it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says in the sacred hadith that His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ related from Him: "I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves. When he says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: 'My servant has praised Me.'" Who says this? The worshipper. Who responds to him? The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, above His Throne, above His heavens, who hears him even if he recites quietly, and says: "My servant has praised Me." Now, the worshippers may number a thousand in the mosque: one says "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds", another is just beginning the opening, another is reciting the end of al-Fatihah or near its end. How is this? We say: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. Each one of them has thousands upon thousands, and even though their words differ, He responds to each: "When he says: 'All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds', He says: 'My servant has praised Me.'" Glory be to Allah the Great! How vast is the greatness of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic! He says: "My servant has praised Me. When he says: ﴿the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾", now He has increased in description. He has described Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as possessing a vast mercy that reaches fully the one who is shown mercy. In His saying "al-Rahman" there is an indication of the vastness of mercy, and in His saying "al-Rahim" there is an indication of its reaching those who receive it: ﴿the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. When a person says it, the Majestic and Exalted responds with: "My servant has extolled Me." "Extolled Me": what is the meaning of "athna"? It means he repeated the praise a second time, because it is derived from "thani", meaning return; that is, he returned a second time to praise Me. "When the servant says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgement﴾", what does the Lord, majestic and exalted, say? He says: "My servant has glorified Me." That is, he has described Me with glory, which is greatness, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgement﴾.
