"When he says: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾", Allah says: "This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks." What is shared between Him and His servant? ﴿You alone we worship﴾ is for Allah, and ﴿You alone we ask for help﴾ is for whom? For the creature: you seek help from Him in all your affairs, in worship, in eating, drinking, sleeping, going out, travelling, and in everything. So they are yours: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾. ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾. Allah said: "This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks." How many verses have we recited? ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds (2). The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate (3). Master of the Day of Judgement (4). You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (5)﴾. How many are these, O brothers? How many?

* The students: Four.

* The Shaykh: How many? Four. ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾: five. ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾: six. ﴿Not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾: how many is that?

* The students: Seven.

* The Shaykh: Seven, exactly. Al-Fatihah has seven verses. ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an﴾ [al-Hijr 87]. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) explained that "the seven oft-repeated" is al-Fatihah [Related by al-Bukhari (4474) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, with the wording: "'All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds' is the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur'an which I have been given."], and it has seven verses. But perhaps some of you have a mushaf in your hands, so review it: you will find that ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾ is one verse. If we make it one verse, and we begin with "Alhamdu", how many verses does it then have? It would have six, and this is problematic.

The answer to that is that the numbering in the printed mushafs today is based on the basmalah being part of al-Fatihah. For this reason the basmalah is marked as number one, and ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ as number two. But the correct view, without doubt, is that the basmalah is not part of al-Fatihah, and that it is a verse that begins the surahs, except for Surah al-Bara'ah. The evidence for this is this hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which is established in the Sahih: "I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves. When he says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾..." and it does not say "When he says: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." So what is the beginning of al-Fatihah? Not the first verse in it; its beginning is ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. Also, the verse which divides the prayer between Allah and His servant into two halves is the verse that divides al-Fatihah exactly in half, because before it there are three verses and after it three verses, so it is half of al-Fatihah. This verse, which is the half, has its first part for Allah and its last part for the servant. Furthermore, if ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾ were two verses, it would be a long verse compared with the preceding verses. But when this last verse is divided into two, ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾ and ﴿not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾, the verses become proportionate in length. So the verbal, the meaningful and the transmitted evidence all indicate that the beginning of al-Fatihah is ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, and that the basmalah is not part of it. For this reason, the correct position is that when a person recites it (that is, recites al-Fatihah in an audibly recited prayer), he should audibly recite al-Fatihah. If I am wrong, correct me. For this reason, the correct position is that when a person recites al-Fatihah in an audibly recited prayer, he audibly recites the basmalah. Is that right or not?

* A student: No, no, Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: My brothers, we said: the basmalah is not part of al-Fatihah. If the basmalah is not part of al-Fatihah, is it recited audibly?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not recited audibly, just as we do not recite the opening audibly because it is outside al-Fatihah. Likewise we do not recite the basmalah audibly. This is the correct position. For this reason Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ, behind Abu Bakr and behind 'Umar, and they did not recite 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' [aloud]." This is in Sahih Muslim [(399/50)]. But the meaning is that they did not recite it audibly, and this hadith is to be understood as meaning that they did not recite it audibly, and that is indeed so.

Let us return, my brothers, once more to this great surah, which the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the seven oft-repeated, and let us consider the meanings it contains, the meanings around which the whole Qur'an revolves. Look, glory be to Allah! In this short surah all the meanings of the Qur'an are gathered. For this reason Allah did not oblige us to recite any surah in the prayer except this one, because it contains all the meanings of the Qur'an. In it are mention of Lordship, divinity, the Names and Attributes, recompense, action, and the divisions of people. Into how many categories are people divided in Surah al-Fatihah?

* A student: Into three.

* The Shaykh: Into three categories. ﴿Guide us to the straight path (6). The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾: this is the first. ﴿Not of those who have earned anger﴾: this is the second. ﴿Nor of those who are astray﴾: the third. So we understand that the categories of people are three: those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, who are those who knew the truth and acted upon it; ﴿those who have earned anger﴾, who are those who knew the truth but did not act upon it, and foremost among them are whom?

* A student: The Jews and the Christians.

* The Shaykh: No, the Jews only. And those who are astray, who were ignorant of the truth and acted upon falsehood, are whom?

* The students: The Christians.

* The Shaykh: The Christians. For this reason Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians." [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (4/138).]

As for the scholar who becomes corrupt, he has known the truth and opposed it, and we seek refuge with Allah. We ask Allah to guide us and you to His straight path. As for the worshippers who have become corrupt: they are eager for good and seek worship, but they are ignorant and worship Allah in misguidance. Such people have a resemblance to whom?

* A student: To the Christians.

* The Shaykh: To the Christians. What, O believer in Allah and His Messenger, is your duty? Your duty is to learn in order to act; to learn in order to act. Learn in order to leave off resembling whom? To leave off resembling whom? Say it, all of you.

* A student: The Christians.

* The Shaykh: The Christians. And act in order to leave off resembling the Jews. Woe to the scholars if they do not act upon what they know; woe to them. They are the likeness of the Jews, and they are the root of misguidance, because the common people follow whom? Their scholars. So if the scholars go astray, they lead others astray. If the scholars go astray, and we seek refuge with Allah, and do not act upon the truth, they lead others astray. We seek refuge with Allah from this state: they lead others astray. And do not think that the scholar is the one who holds a doctorate, or who graduates from a college, or who keeps company with the scholars so that it is said, "So-and-so is a student of knowledge." Whoever knows one issue is a scholar in that issue; that is, if you learn a single matter, you are a scholar of it. For this reason our imam and our prophet, Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), said, what did he say? He said: "Convey from me, even if it is one verse" [Related by al-Bukhari (3461) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both)]. Did he say: convey from me only if you are great scholars? Answer, all of you.

* The students: No.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 1, verse 1–7 (part 3 of 9):

* The Shaykh: He said, "Convey from me, even if it is one verse." Therefore, whoever memorizes a single ruling of the religion of Allah, the proof is established against him by that ruling, and it becomes obligatory for him to act upon it, and obligatory for him to convey it: "Convey from me, even if it is one verse." But be keen to understand the truth as it is, and do not err in understanding, because many people err in understanding on the basis of their own assumptions. Even among the Companions some erred in understanding, O brothers. A person is not infallible from error in understanding.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) and laid down his battle gear, Jibril came to him and commanded him to go out to Banu Qurayzah. Who are Banu Qurayzah? A tribe of the Jews who betrayed and deceived the Prophet (ﷺ). Jibril commanded him to go out to Banu Qurayzah, so the Prophet (ﷺ) called his Companions to set out and said to them: "None of you should pray the 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (946) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).]] Do you think that one of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said: (...) "We will pray when we arrive, and we will rise at dawn"? Did they say that? No, they did not say that. I appreciate the one who stays silent when he has no knowledge, but we all know that the state of the Companions could not be like that. When he said, "None of you should pray the 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah," they all set out, and the time of 'Asr came upon them. They divided into two groups. One group followed the text literally and said: "We will not pray 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah, even if it is in the middle of the night. We cannot pray 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah, because the Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'None of you should pray the 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah.'" So they did not pray, and even if the sun set, they did not pray. Others said: The Messenger (ﷺ) said this, but he did not say: Do not pray 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah. Rather, he meant: delay 'Asr. What did he mean by it?
* The students: Hastening.
* The Shaykh: That we should hasten and rush, so that 'Asr does not come upon us except while we are in Banu Qurayzah. I think this style of speech exists now too: if I want to send you to a certain town, I say: "Look, dawn should not break except while you are in such-and-such town," or "Do not pray Fajr except there." What is the meaning?
That is, does he sit and sleep and not pray Fajr until Dhuhr?! No, the meaning is: hurry.

The Companions differed in understanding, O brothers, they differed, and the one who is correct according to the preponderant view of the scholars is the one who prayed on time.

The Prophet (ﷺ) made an oath (ila') concerning the Mothers of the Believers for a month, swearing that he would not have relations with his wives for a full month. What is the meaning of ila'? It means he swore. The Prophet (ﷺ) swore that he would not have relations with them for a full month. This was a significant event in the eyes of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). The news spread that the Messenger (ﷺ) had divorced his wives, until 'Umar came, entered the mosque, and found people near the pulpit saying: "The Messenger (ﷺ) has divorced his wives." But 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) afterwards verified the matter and entered upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and found that there was no divorce, only withdrawal (i'tizal) for a month. Those who told 'Umar that the Messenger had divorced his wives meant that they did not fully understand the story, did they not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: I say, returning to my first point: whoever knows a ruling must verify his understanding of it before conveying it to the people. He should not take it superficially and then go and convey it, for he may convey it wrongly. Rather, verify the matter from a scholar, or, if you are able, extract it from the books: from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), and what relates to them of tafsir or explanation. When you have verified that it is true, then convey it and call the people to it.

I say: O brothers, this great surah (al-Fatihah) includes all the meanings of the Noble Quran, and for this reason it is called, by the Prophet's (ﷺ) naming, what?
* The students: Umm al-Quran (the Mother of the Quran).
* The Shaykh: It is called Umm al-Quran and Umm al-Kitab. The "umm" (mother) of a thing is its source to which it returns, as the poet said:
"Upon its head is a mother we follow..." ...............................
That is, a sign we head toward and aim for. When you say in al-Fatihah: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, what does it mean? Who can answer me on the meaning of ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾? We all recite it, O my brothers.
* A student: Praise.
* The Shaykh: Its meaning is complete praise with the most perfect attributes, deserved by whom?
* The students: By Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: By Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, what is the meaning of "Lord of the worlds"? The Rabb is the Creator, the Owner, the Manager. And the "'alam" (worlds), who are they? Please, give us the meaning of "'alam," what is the meaning of 'alam?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Eh, the one beside him.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Subhan Allah! The 'alam, ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾? If I say to you: Lord of creation, you know what creation is?
* A student: Whatever is other than Allah.
* The Shaykh: Whatever is other than Allah. So the 'alam, ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, means all created beings. Is that right or not?
* The students: Correct.
* The Shaykh: We have understood "Lord of the worlds," meaning that I describe Allah with the most perfect attributes, because He is the Lord of the worlds, may He be exalted.

Now, ﴿the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾. What is the meaning of "al-Rahman al-Rahim"? The scholars said: the meaning of al-Rahman is one of vast mercy; al-Rahman means vast in mercy, because the form "fa'lan" indicates fullness and expansiveness. When we see someone whose veins have swollen, whose eyes have reddened, and who has become enraged, what do we say? We say: ghadban (angry), meaning filled with anger. Notice that the form "fa'lan" indicates fullness. Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, possesses vast mercy.
"Al-Rahim": what is its meaning? Al-Rahim means the one who conveys mercy to whomever He wills.
﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-'Ankabut 21]. Thus these two noble names combine the description of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with vastness of mercy, and that this mercy has reached His believing and non-believing servants, because Allah, may He be exalted, has mercy on whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. There is the general mercy, which is the mercy of this world, for believers and disbelievers alike: the disbeliever is shown mercy, Allah provides for him, sustains him and gives him respite. But in the Hereafter he has no mercy: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses﴾ [al-A'raf 156].

﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾: a question, what does it mean? What is the Day of Judgment? You all recite it, O brothers, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾. It means the Master of the Day of Resurrection, in which is the recompense for deeds. The question is: does Allah not own this world?
* A student: He owns it.
* The Shaykh: He owns the world and the religion; everything is owned by Him, Mighty and Majestic. But He mentioned the Day of Judgment, the Day of Resurrection, because no one has ownership on that day, as Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir 16]. In this world we have kings, do we not? We have kings whom Allah has placed over us, but in the Hereafter there is no owner except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. There is no owner among the creation at all. For this reason we say: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾.

Do you know what our saying ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ includes? It includes belief in the Last Day and belief in recompense for deeds, and that the One who recompenses deeds is who?
* The students: Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
* The Shaykh: Allah is the Master of the Day of Judgment.

﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾.
First: I ask, what is worship ('ibadah)? I will not permit the students of knowledge to answer it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, no, I do not permit the student of knowledge to answer it, (...) a student of knowledge. What is 'ibadah? Answer it by example. Say: such as such, not by definition. We designate someone to answer. Worship is like what?
* A student: Prayer.
* The Shaykh: Excellent. Worship is like prayer. Prayer is worship, is it not?
* The students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And zakah?
* The students: It is worship.
* The Shaykh: It is worship. Fasting, Hajj, wudu', all of it is worship. So from these many examples we conclude that everything Allah has commanded in order to draw near to Him is worship. So 'ibadah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah has commanded for the purpose of drawing near to Him. And the phrase "for the purpose of drawing near to Him" is included because Allah may command us to do something not for drawing near to Him, but for our own benefit: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive﴾ [al-A'raf 31], ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2], and what is similar to that. The original ruling of these commands is permissibility. Yet eating and drinking may become worship. How can you make your dinner tonight an act of worship, O brother?
* The student: If you intend by it to strengthen your body for obedience to Allah.
* The Shaykh: Eating and drinking can become worship. How? When you eat while intending to comply with the command of Allah, it is worship, is it not?
Now, when you eat to protect yourself from harm, is it worship? Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa' 29]. And if a person did not eat until he died of hunger... When you eat to enjoy the blessing of Allah upon you, is it worship? How is it worship? Enjoying the blessing of Allah upon you can be worship?!
Yes, because when Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon him. And because the generous person loves that his generosity be enjoyed. Does he love it or not?
* The students: He loves it.
* The Shaykh: If a generous man among you served you food, would he like you to eat it and not leave it?
* The students: We eat it.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. But if a stingy man served you bread... we would not say, it is not flatbread, but bread. Perhaps we would say: two people eat only one piece, so that he can take back the remaining bread.
So the generous person loves that people enjoy his generosity, and now when you eat you love to enjoy the generosity of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and this without doubt brings you closer to Allah.
Fourth: if you intend by your eating to seek help in obedience to Allah, what happens?
* The students: It is worship.
* The Shaykh: It becomes worship. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take the pre-dawn meal (suhur), for in suhur there is blessing."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (1923) and Muslim (1095/45) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him).]]
So, O brothers, let us return to the noble verse ﴿You alone we worship﴾. What is worship? Every deed by which a person draws near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And You alone we ask for help﴾: what is the meaning of "nasta'in" (we seek help)? What is the meaning of seeking help? Your car got stuck in the sand; you have oil nearby. Your car got stuck in the sand, and you saw two, three, or four people walking, and you said: "Come and help me with it." What is this called?
* The students: Seeking help (isti'anah).
The Shaykh: Seeking help. So ﴿And You alone we ask for help﴾ means: we ask You for help in what? In worship and in all matters. ﴿And You alone we ask for help﴾, that is, we ask You for help.

﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾. The noble verse says ﴿Guide us to the path﴾ and did not say "guide us to the path" with "ila"; Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura 52], without saying "ṣiraṭan mustaqiman" with a preposition; but He also said to His Prophet: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath 2].
What is the difference between "hadahu ila al-ṣirat" (he guided him to the path) and "hadahu al-ṣirat" (he guided him the path)? The difference: "hadahu ila al-ṣirat" means he pointed him to it only, as a mere indication, while "hadahu al-ṣirat" means he guided him to it and into it. For this reason the preposition is omitted, so that it is general.
So the meaning of ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ is: show us it and enable us to act upon it. Thus in this supplication you are asking Allah for beneficial knowledge, and what else?
* The students: And action.
* The Shaykh: And righteous action. Then ﴿al-Mustaqim﴾ (the straight). ﴿al-Ṣirat al-Mustaqim﴾. Is there a crooked path? Yes. Everything that departs from the religion of Allah is a crooked path: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am 153]. So everything that takes you out of the way of Allah is other than the straight path.

Following the muezzin is a emphasized Sunnah: you say what he says, except in "hayya 'ala al-salah" and "hayya 'ala al-falah," where you say: "la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." The meaning of "la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" is seeking help from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; that is, you disavow power and strength except through Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If Allah does not strengthen you to obey Him, you cannot. And the muezzin says "hayy" meaning what?
* A student: Come.
* The Shaykh: That is, come. Coming to obedience requires the help of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, so you say: "la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." And in the muezzin's saying in the Fajr prayer, "al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm" (prayer is better than sleep), you say: "al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm," because the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Say the like of what he says."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (611) and Muslim (383/10) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him).]] The Sunnah did not report an exception except in "hayya 'ala al-salah" and "hayya 'ala al-falah." As for the view of some scholars that you say "sadaqta wa barirta" (you have spoken truly and righteously), there is no basis for it. Without doubt he is truthful in his saying "al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm," just as he is truthful in saying "Allahu akbar," but we say: you say the like of what he says, "al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm."

If you are in prayer, do you answer the muezzin?
* A student: No (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, you do not answer the muezzin, because you are occupied with your prayer. But when you finish, the scholars said: the one praying and the one in the toilet (al-mutakhalli, the one in the lavatory) both postpone it; they postpone following the muezzin. When you finish, you say: "Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad, Allahumma rabba hadhihi al-da'wah al-tammah wa al-salah al-qa'imah, a'ti Muhammadan al-wasilah wa al-fadilah wa u'thhu maqaman mahmudan alladhi wa'adtahu, innaka la tukhlifu al-mee'ad" (O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad; O Lord of this perfect call and this established prayer, grant Muhammad the wasilah and the excellence, and raise him to the praised station which You have promised him, for You never break Your promise).[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4719) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (1933), and the wording with this addition "innaka la tukhlif al-mi'ad" is from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Do you answer the muezzin during the sermon? During the Friday prayer sermon? If you say: no, you are wrong; if you say: yes, you are wrong. Do you answer the muezzin while the imam is delivering the sermon on Friday?
* A student: It is not contrary.
* The Shaykh: The answer: there is no adhan on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon.
* A student: There is no adhan at the time of Friday. There is no adhan at the sermon.
* The Shaykh: But there is no adhan while the imam is delivering the sermon except when it is in another mosque. I tell you, perhaps.

Now, if you enter on Friday while the muezzin is calling the adhan, do you pray tahiyyat al-masjid (greeting of the mosque) or do you answer the muezzin and, after finishing, pray the greeting of the mosque?
Some scholars said: you answer the muezzin, and after finishing you pray the greeting of the mosque. Others say: you pray the greeting of the mosque and listen to the sermon, because listening to the sermon is more important, since listening to the sermon is obligatory, while answering the muezzin, according to the preponderant view, is not obligatory. This is one aspect. Another aspect: if you hasten and perform the two rak'ahs while he is calling the adhan, it is better; hastening with them is better than delaying. In any case, what I call myself and you to is that we do not miss this opportunity: we follow the muezzin and say what he says, except in the two hay'alas, then we send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then we say: "Allahumma rabba hadhihi al-da'wah al-tammah," and so on to its end. Whoever does that, what is his reward? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My intercession becomes due for him on the Day of Resurrection."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (614) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him).]] O Allah, make us among them.

Let us return to al-Fatihah, and I feel that I am completing the prayer, but I do not know, perhaps (...) we do not complete all the pillars of the prayer.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Guide us to the straight path (6), the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾.
Who are those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor? We can ask someone who knows, who has recited the Quran. Good.

**Student:** ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ [An-Nisa 69].

**Shaykh:** Yes. Your brother says: the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor are those mentioned in His saying, ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor﴾. Who are they? ﴿Of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾

How many categories? Four categories. The Qur'an explains itself. So if someone asks you, "Who are those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor?", recite to him the verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾ The prophets include the messengers, because every messenger is a prophet, but not vice versa. The steadfast in truth (ṣiddīqūn) are like Abu Bakr. The martyrs are like ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, and many others, but this is by way of example.

The Prophet (ﷺ) climbed Mount Uhud, and many of you know Mount Uhud. Where is it located? In Makkah?

**Students:** In Madinah.

**Shaykh:** In Madinah? Yes, in Madinah. The Prophet (ﷺ) climbed it, and the mountain shook beneath the Messenger (ﷺ), along with Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, four men, and the mountain shook with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be still, O Uhud, for upon you are a prophet, a steadfast in truth, and two martyrs."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3699) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him).]] May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the Messenger of Allah. Allahu Akbar! The mountain shook. It appears to me – and Allah knows best, and knowledge is with Allah – that it shook out of joy at those who stood upon its back, or to manifest one of the signs of Allah. Then he said: "Be still, O Uhud, for upon you are a prophet, a steadfast in truth, and two martyrs." The steadfast in truth is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and the two martyrs are ʿUmar and ʿUthmān. ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) was the martyr of the prayer. He was stabbed while standing before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Whenever he entered the mosque, he would straighten the rows, just as our imam and our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) used to straighten the rows. Do you know how the Messenger (ﷺ) would straighten them? He would straighten them with his hand, passing his hand over the shoulders and chests until they were perfectly even. When the people increased, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān appointed men to inspect the rows, and when they came and said, "The rows are straight," then he would say the takbir. You may find it strange when some imams delay and say, "Straighten up," and straighten the rows themselves, but there is nothing strange in this. In the narration of Abu Dawud, he says: "When we had straightened, he would say the takbir."[[(665) from the hadith of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr (may Allah be pleased with him).]] When he (ʿUmar) advanced and began the takbir for the Fajr prayer, he (may Allah be pleased with him) cried out and said: "The dog has eaten me!"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3700).]] He did not mean the ordinary dog, this one; he meant this wicked one who is more wicked than a dog, and that was Abu Lu'lu'ah al-Majusi (the Magian). Because the Magians, without doubt, harbor resentment in their hearts toward whom?

**Students:** Toward the Shariʿah of Islam, and especially toward ʿUmar, under whose hands Allah brought down the palace of Kisra (Khosrow). So he stabbed ʿUmar with a dagger that had two edges and a handle in the middle, because he was a wicked man seeking to harm, so whenever anyone came near him, he struck this way and that. But the Companions caught up with him, and he stabbed more than ten people, until they threw a cloth over him, and he took his own life, and we seek refuge with Allah. ʿUmar was the martyr of the prayer, and ʿUthmān was the martyr of the Mushaf (Qur'an codex). The Kharijites entered upon him while he was reciting, and they killed him in his house. Some historians even mention that a drop of his blood fell upon the verse of Allah, ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah 137].

"Be still, O Uhud; upon you are a prophet, a steadfast in truth, and two martyrs." But you may ask: how could the Messenger (ﷺ), who is the most intelligent of people, address an inanimate object and say to it, "Be still"? The answer: this inanimate object has understanding. The evidence is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their exaltation﴾ [Al-Isra 44]. Does everything glorify Allah through the tongue of disposition (lisan al-hal) or through the tongue of speech (lisan al-maqal)?

**Students:** (...).

**Shaykh:** Through both the tongue of disposition and the tongue of speech, except for disbelievers among the children of Adam and the jinn, who glorify Allah through the tongue of disposition without the tongue of speech. Also, the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Uhud is a mountain that loves us, and we love it."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (2889) and Muslim (1365/462), and his wording is: "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it."]] Allahu Akbar! Great wisdom. If this place existed in the time of the later generations, they would regard it as ill-omened, because what befell the Muslims there – martyrdom, killing, wounding, fatigue, and hardship – took place there. I say: if these later people had this place, they would consider it ill-omened. But the Messenger said about Uhud: "A mountain that loves us," and it is not strange that the Messenger of Allah and the believers love it. But "and we love it" – does this ascribe will to the mountain or not? What is it? Love. An inanimate object loves the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. Also, perhaps some of you have heard the story that happened to Musa (Moses), peace be upon him. Musa, the Prophet of Allah, and the Children of Israel used to bathe naked, looking at one another, but Musa (ﷺ) never bathed naked, never bathed in anyone's presence. What did the Children of Israel say? They said: "Musa has some defect; otherwise he would not conceal himself from us when bathing. Indeed, Musa is ādar." What is the meaning of (ādar)? It means one with a large testicle. See, and we seek refuge with Allah, how the Children of Israel said this about their Prophet!

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, willed a matter that was not Musa's choice. Musa entered to bathe one day and placed his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment. It ran off! Allahu Akbar! So Musa followed it, running after it, saying: "My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!"[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (3404) and Muslim (339/75) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]] That is, (...) his garment; he was addressing the rock. How could he address it when it is a rock? Because the rock ran off with his garment, fled with it until it reached the assembly of the Children of Israel, and they saw Musa, and behold, Musa was sound and innocent of what they had said. ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said﴾ [Al-Ahzab 69]. So Musa was sound, peace be upon him. When the people saw him, the rock stopped. Then Musa took his garment and began striking the rock. How could he strike it when it is a rock? Because in Musa's view it had wronged him by fleeing with his garment, and it had caused the Children of Israel to look at his private parts. I do not know whether, when we were young, we used to grind something with a stone. When we were children and ground something with a stone, the mother would come and strike the stone, saying, "Let me grind it so that it quiets you." Is this of the same kind or not?

**Shaykh:** No, because that was a sign from the signs of Allah, but this (the stone your mother strikes) is something whose state we do not know; it is unknown to us.

﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.﴾ You may ask: would it not suffice to say, ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾, since those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor are the four categories who knew the truth and acted upon it? So why did it come with ﴿not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray﴾? We say: this is for the sake of emphasizing the completeness of the affirmed matter. And what is the affirmed matter? ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor.﴾ So that there is not even a small portion of the path of those who have evoked anger and those who are astray in this path. This is for the sake of emphasizing completeness. I think many students of knowledge now understand that the negative attributes of Allah imply the affirmation of the perfection of their opposites. So when it is said, ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf 49], the meaning is that, because of His perfect justice, there is no injustice in His action or in His judgment.

Therefore ﴿not of those who have evoked [Your] anger﴾ comes for the sake of the perfection of that affirmation in His saying, ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾, so that there is in this guidance no trace of misguidance and no cause of anger. I ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to benefit me and you by what we have heard from this great surah, which comprehensively includes the meanings of the Qur'an. In truth, if anyone is able to read this surah with deep reflection and examination, and by reviewing the words of the scholars concerning it, he will find in it very great meanings. For this reason it is the "Mother of the Book" which must be recited in every rak'ah of the prayer. Moreover, it is a great ruqyah (protective recitation) for a person.

One day the Companions, while on an expedition (sariyyah) that the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent them on, stopped at a people and asked them for hospitality. These Companions requested hospitality from this group, but they did not provide it to them. This is meanness and stinginess. The Arabs in their pre-Islamic period used to honor the guest, but these people did not honor the expedition of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he had sent out.

What happened? The Mighty, the All-Wise, Majestic and Exalted, decreed that their chief was stung by a snake. They looked for someone who could recite. They said: "Perhaps among these travelers who have come there is someone who recites. Send them to us." So they came to them and said: "Is there anyone among you who recites?" They said: "Yes, there is someone among us who recites." They said: "Recite for our master or companion." They said: "We will not recite unless we are paid. You neglected your duty, and it was incumbent upon you to provide hospitality; we will not recite except for a wage." They said: "We will give you this flock of sheep, this herd of goats." They said: "Very well, then we will recite." So one of them went to this stung man and began reciting over him al-Fatihah, the Chapter of the Opening. Then the stung man, who had been bitten by what? A small ant, is that right or not? A scorpion? A hornet? A snake. A snake! He rose as soon as he recited al-Fatihah, as though he had been released from a tether. What is the meaning of (released from a tether)? It means like a camel whose rope was untied, so he stood up, with nothing but well-being, and only by the recitation of al-Fatihah. But the Companions, out of their scrupulousness, said: "We cannot eat from this flock until we return to the Messenger (ﷺ) and ask him." So they asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Take it" or he said: "Eat, and set aside a share for me with you."[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (2276) and Muslim (2201/66) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him).]] Glory be to Allah! See, he said: "Set aside a share for me with you." Why? So that they would be reassured, because when the mufti (jurist) does what he issues as a ruling, that brings greater reassurance to the one who asks. For this reason, it is related about Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) that when the Tatars besieged Damascus during Ramadan, the scholars said: "You cannot break your fast," and they told the soldiers: "You cannot break your fast. You are not ill nor traveling, and we see no concession for you to break the fast. Fight while you are fasting." They said: "O people, we are exhausted." They said: "Fight, and do not break your fast. Allah says: ﴿Whoever among you is ill or on a journey [may make up the days]﴾ [Al-Baqarah 184]. You are neither ill nor traveling." But Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "No, break your fast. Break your fast and eat, so that you may gain strength through it for the fighting." He derived this (may Allah have mercy on him, and reward him on behalf of Islam with good) from the Conquest campaign. We all know that the Messenger went out to the Conquest in which month? In Ramadan. The people fasted, and he commanded them to break their fast. Then when they drew near their enemy, he said: "You will meet the enemy tomorrow, so break your fast, for breaking the fast is stronger for you."[[Narrated by Muslim (1120/102) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), and his wording is: "You will be facing your enemy at dawn, and breaking the fast is stronger for you; so break your fast."]] He did not say: "Because you are travelers." Breaking the fast is stronger; "You will meet the enemy tomorrow, so break your fast, for breaking the fast is stronger for you." So the Companions broke their fast. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him, and reward him on behalf of Islam with good) was among the soldiers, and he was a brave man and a scholar. He walked among the soldiers in Ramadan carrying a piece of bread, eating it in front of the people, so that—

So that they would be reassured and know that this man issued the ruling out of conviction. And this is what the Messenger (ﷺ) did before him; he was following the example of the Messenger (ﷺ), who said: "Set aside a share for me with you." Then he said to the one who recited al-Fatihah over that stung man: "How do you know that it is a ruqyah?" That it is a ruqyah. So what is the best thing we should recite over our sick and over whoever among us is afflicted in such matters?

**Students:** Al-Fatihah.

**Shaykh:** Al-Fatihah. But we ask Allah to have mercy on our weakness. It may happen that someone recites al-Fatihah twenty times and the patient does not benefit. Why? Is it because al-Fatihah is not the same as the first al-Fatihah, or because the reciter is not the same reciter? The reciter is not the same reciter.

Recitation benefits only with three conditions: the receptivity of the subject (qabiliyyat al-mahall), the competence of the reciter (ahliyyat al-qari'), and the validity of the recitation (salahiyyat al-qira'ah). So if a person recites what is not valid of these incantations (ʿazaʾim) and the like, it does not benefit. And if the person over whom it is recited is not receptive, which is what we call the receptivity of the subject, it does not benefit. For example, if you recite over a patient and the patient doubts, saying, "By Allah, I do not know about this recitation; I will go to the hospital, that is better," does he benefit or not?

He does not benefit. And if the reciter is not competent, it also does not benefit. So there must be competence in the reciter, receptivity in the subject, and validity of what is recited, meaning that it is established by the Shariʿah; otherwise it does not benefit. If you recite a thousand times while you are in doubt, it will not benefit you. Incidentally, I want to point out that the Messenger (ﷺ) informed that "whoever recites the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) on a night, there will remain over him a guardian from Allah, and no devil will come near him until morning."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2311) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]] So one should recite it every night, but with faith. Not everyone says, "I want to test whether it benefits or not." Whoever says, "I want to test," that means doubt. A person should recite it with faith, believing that when he recites it, there will remain over him a guardian from Allah, and no devil will come near him until morning. The Verse of the Throne is well known at the beginning of the third part of the Qur'an.

Perhaps Shaykh 'Abdullah now has some questions in hand, so let us limit ourselves to this. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant us and you beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and to take our souls in faith. O Allah, send blessings and peace upon the Messenger of Allah.

**Student:** May Allah reward Your Eminence, our Shaykh, with all good on our behalf, prolong his life in righteous deeds, benefit us by what we have heard, and place what he has said in the scales of his good deeds on the day he meets Allah, glorified and exalted.

**Shaykh:** Amin.

**Student:** Dear brothers, the questions are very numerous, and the brothers who sorted the questions were keen to include most of them. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to grant the Shaykh success in answering all that has been sorted from them.

**Shaykh:** And upon what is correct.

**Student:** And upon what is correct, God willing. May He guide him to what is correct in speech.

**Student:** This is a young woman who asks: "On my forehead there is a mole (shāmah) on the brow, and it covers the entire brow, and I want to remove it by surgery. Is that permissible or not?"

**Shaykh:** In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Answer:** Yes. If a person has a defect in their physical makeup, they may remove that defect. So if the mole is on the forehead, as the questioner described, and it covers the forehead or most of it, or it disfigures the appearance, then she may have it removed by surgery, on condition that no harm comes to her body. If doctors say that removing it by surgery is possible, there is no harm in that. The same applies if a person has overlapping teeth, where one tooth sits on top of another, and this hurts them when eating or disfigures their appearance: there is no blame on them for removing the overlapping tooth. As for beautifying teeth by filing and reshaping them, making them smaller, this is forbidden and is even among the major sins, because the Prophet (ﷺ) «cursed the woman who files her teeth and the woman who has them filed»[[Narrated by Ahmad (3945) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and by al-Baghandi in Musnad Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (29, 84) from the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him both; the wording is his.]]. There is a difference between a person acquiring something to beautify themselves and doing something to remove a defect. Removing a defect is not objectionable, but adding beautification is not permitted. The Prophet (ﷺ) permitted a man whose nose had been cut off to have a nose made of silver, but it became foul-smelling, so he had a nose made of gold instead.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4232) and al-Tirmidhi (1770) from the hadith of Arfaja ibn As'ad.]]

* **The student:** May Allah reward you with good. O Shaykh, there has been much talk about plaques on which Qur'anic verses are written. Is it permissible to sell and buy them? And if a Muslim has become entangled in buying one, must the seller take it back from him, or should he sell it, or what should he do with it? Benefit us, may Allah reward you.
* **The Shaykh:** To answer this question: first, the reality is that there are many different plaques, all of which come to us as new things in our religion. They did not exist in the time of the Companions or of those who followed them, the Followers, who are the best generations. Hanging them on walls to decorate the wall is without doubt a degradation of the Speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. How can you make the Speech of Allah, which is the most noble speech, into designs in your house? Hanging them for blessing (tabarruk) is also an innovation (bid'ah). The Companions did not seek blessing from the Qur'an in this way. Hanging them to protect and guard you is also an innovation, for the Companions did not seek protection through what they hung in their houses. Furthermore, it prevents a person from the prescribed act, which is to recite the Qur'an. He himself says: "Instead of reciting the Verse of the Throne every night, I hang it in the room, and that is enough." In addition, there is another kind of degradation of the Qur'an, because this room may be a place of wrongdoing. There may be backbiting or forbidden play or the like, and so this involves a kind of mockery of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. A ruling has been issued by the Permanent Committee for Scientific Research prohibiting such a thing. Even worse, there are small vessels on which the Verse of the Throne is written, engraved in relief. This is without doubt a degradation of the Qur'an: a vessel that is thrown on the ground, and perhaps struck with the foot, and perhaps taken by a small child... It is written on with a verse of the greatest verses, indeed the greatest verse in the Book of Allah, the Verse of the Throne. What I see is that it should not be hung at all. If a person has any of these, he should burn it, and there is no blame on him for doing so, because the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, burned the copies of the Qur'an upon which they had agreed to differ, meaning those in which there was no disagreement, but there were some surahs placed before others, some dialects, and the like. If a person bought them before he knew the ruling, the purchase is valid, because he did not know that it was forbidden, and he thought it was permissible. But, as I said, he should burn it now. If it is not possible to burn it, he should obliterate it by spraying it with paint until the writing disappears. There is also something else that some people hang: some of these plaques have written on them "Allah" on the right and "Muhammad" on the left. Does this exist or not?
* **Student:** It exists.
* **The Shaykh:** Now, a person who looks at this plaque says: "Allah and Muhammad are equal, and Muhammad is a rival (nidd) to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." We ask Allah for well-being! Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has no rival. For this reason, when a man said to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "What Allah wills and you will," what did the Messenger say to him? He said: «Have you made me an equal to Allah?!» The interrogative here is for denial: «Have you made me an equal to Allah?! Rather, what Allah alone wills.»[[Narrated by Ahmad (1839) from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him both; its wording is: «Have you made me and Allah an equal?! Rather, what Allah alone wills.»]] How can we have in front of us "Allah - Muhammad", as if it were written "The King - The Crown Prince"? Is this correct? This is wrong. It is absolutely not permitted to hang this, and it must be removed and broken, because it is clear that it contains shirk. Would you be pleased to hang in your house something that includes association of partners with Allah? I do not think anyone would be pleased with that. Then, even if you hung only the word "Allah", just "Allah", I fear that this word is taken from the Sufis. How do the Sufis mention Allah? They say: "Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah." The extreme among them do not say "Allah". It is not correct to say "Allah"; if you say "Allah" you have associated partners or negated attributes. What should I say? They say: "He, He, He, He, He." What is the meaning of "He, He" in their terms? It means the whole universe. For this reason the Sufis lead their followers to say unity of existence (wahdat al-wujud), we ask Allah for well-being, that the universe is one thing: the Lord is the one being lord over, and the Creator is the created. Therefore I say first: my rejection of these banners is when Allah is paired with Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, for this is a kind of shirk and must be removed. If only "Allah" is written, this is not prescribed, and it is an innovation. What is the meaning of your saying "Allah" only? Or even if you say "Allah, Majestic in His Majesty," what is the meaning of this?

  So all of this has come from these ignorant people, from the Pakistanis and others, who have made such things into merchandise, because the emotions of Muslims love Islam, love Allah, love the Messenger, and love to see the name of Allah and the name of the Messenger. But in worship there must be following (ittiba'), not innovation (ibtida'). What I advise my Muslim brothers is to leave all of that. And do not think that when I gave the example that these come from Pakistan, that means they are specific to those people. No, they come from Pakistan and from other than Pakistan. They may come from several directions. What concerns us is not whether they come from this place or that place, but whether they agree with the Sharia or not.
* **Student:** Alright, what about writing verses in mosques?
* **The Shaykh:** The ruling on mosques and other places is the same. Writing verses in mosques: it is true that a place is generally not degraded, although a mosque may be degraded. There are some good brothers who come to the mosque and sit with one another, and they are good people, and then they speak about the honour of people. Is this not found? Perhaps it is found. I do not say it is found one hundred percent, but it may be found. Speaking about people's honour is among the major sins, a major sin, and it is not forgiven except with repentance. Prayer, fasting, Hajj, and Umrah do not expiate it; it is expiated only by repentance. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them.» Who knows the completion of the hadith? «As long as the major sins are avoided.»[[Narrated by Muslim (233/16) from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Backbiting (ghibah) is among the major sins. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And let not some of you backbite others.﴾ Complete the verse: ﴿Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ [al-Hujurat 12]. Imagine this situation: your brother, whether in religion or by lineage, has been presented to you dead. Is it possible that you would cut off his flesh and eat it? Tell me: is it possible or not?
* **The students:** No.
* **The Shaykh:** Never, impossible. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So you would detest it.﴾ The one who backbites his brother is like the one who eats his flesh when dead. Why did He not say "to eat the flesh of his brother alive"? Why did He say ﴿dead﴾? Because the one being backbitten is not present and cannot defend himself, just as the dead cannot defend himself. And in order to emphasize the repulsion from this blameworthy trait... May Allah guide us all, save us from people, and save people from us. We find that many people, people of goodness and religion, do not care about backbiting others.
* **The student:** May Allah reward you, O Shaykh. We often hear about transplanting organs, exchanging them, selling them, and donating them. What is the ruling on that, may Allah reward you with good?
* **The Shaykh:** The ruling on this has been issued by the Council of Senior Scholars, as far as I think, and I think it was published in the journal Al-Buhuth. As for the scholars of the Hanbali school, may Allah have mercy on them, they stated explicitly that this is forbidden. They said: it is not permissible to cut off a limb from a dead person even if he bequeathed it. This was mentioned by the author of al-Iqna' in the book of funerals, because the human being is honoured, and the person himself is a trust (amanah) with him. If someone said: "My body is mine; I want to burn it with fire," what would happen? Is that forbidden or permitted?
* **The students:** Forbidden, forbidden.
* **The Shaykh:** Forbidden. If he said: "My body is mine; I want to slaughter it," we would say: do it, and you will be punished in the Fire of Hell with the same means by which you killed yourself. It is forbidden for you.
  So you have no right to dispose of any part of your body, even after your death. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Breaking the bone of a dead person is like breaking it while he is alive.»[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3207) and Ibn Majah (1616) from the hadith of Aisha. Abu Dawud narrated it with a sound chain.]] However, we say: since this matter has been ruled upon by the people of knowledge in our country, these are matters of ijtihad. Whoever it becomes clear to, let him follow the truth, and let him not dispute with anyone who differs with him, unless there is a consensus (ijma') on the matter, for the consensus of the Ummah is protected from error.
* **The student:** May Allah reward you, O Shaykh. After the Eid prayer, people have become accustomed to embracing one another, even if they came together. What is the ruling on that?
* **The Shaykh:** This is not from the Sunnah, and I do not know of any Sunnah on this from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, nor from the Companions. I think this is one of the customary matters, not one of the acts of worship. So if people embrace one another or shake hands and congratulate one another, I hope there is no harm in that. As for kissing, this has no basis and is not well known. Kissing is prescribed only for a reason, such as returning from a journey, or showing mercy to a sick person, or the like. Without a reason it is not prescribed, and so it is not prescribed for you to kiss your companion every time you meet him. This is not prescribed.
* **The student:** What is the ruling on visiting graves on the day of Eid? And what is the ruling on embracing inside the graveyard? And what is the ruling on...?
* **The Shaykh:** Inside the graveyard, meaning at the burial?
* **The student:** At the burial. And what is the ruling on saying, after the burial: "May Allah establish it and perpetuate it as long as the heavens and earth endure"?
* **The Shaykh:** Visiting graves on the day of Eid has no basis at all, and it is not prescribed. Whoever believes it to be a Sunnah has innovated in the religion of Allah something that is not part of it. For this reason, we should advise one another about this matter, and if we see someone going out to the graves on the day of Eid, we should say to him: "O brother, this is not prescribed, so do not do it, because when you do it, people will believe it is a Sunnah, and it is not a Sunnah. Customs in worship are unacceptable and rejected." That is, customs in matters intended as worship are rejected until it is established that they are acts of worship. Is visiting graves one of the acts of worship or one of the pure customs?
* **The student:** One of the acts of worship.
* **The Shaykh:** One of the acts of worship. That is, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded it. If it is one of the acts of worship, then let us look: was it part of the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ) that on the day of Eid he would go out to the graves to visit them?
  No. He did not command it, and he did not guide the Ummah to it. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, used to command visiting graves, and he would go out to them to visit them, sometimes even at night. So I ask you, may Allah bless you, not to go out to the graves on the day of Eid to visit them, and to guide anyone who does that, and to say: "This, O brother, is not a Sunnah. Do not exhaust yourself without benefit, or with something harmful to you." As for embracing after the burial, this is also an innovation with no basis and no justification at all. In fact, I have some reservation about shaking hands at condolences, because a person may be beside you, and you will not meet him again. But if you meet your believing brother, shake his hand. However, if you are beside him and then, after the deceased has been buried, you go to shake his hand, I know of no basis for this at all. As for embracing and kissing, they have no basis whatsoever, and they are forbidden. Know that condolence is given before the burial and after the burial, contrary to what some of the common people think, that it is only after the burial. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, offered condolences to his daughter before her child died. One of his daughters sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him to come, because her child, a boy or a girl, was at the point of death. So the messenger came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to inform him of his daughter's request that he come. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to the messenger, and note the great words of condolence, which are better than what we say: he said to the messenger: «Tell her to be patient and to seek reward, for to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He leaves, and everything with Him has a specified term.»[[A hadith agreed upon: al-Bukhari (7377) and Muslim (932/11) from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd.]] Allahu Akbar, how great these words are! «Let her be patient»: let her restrain herself from discontent. She should not tear her garments, slap her cheeks, pull out her hair, or complain. «And let her seek reward»: what does "seek reward" mean? It means to expect the reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Only the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾ [al-Zumar 10]. Look at these words: «To Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He leaves.» The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, spoke the truth. To whom does the dominion belong?
* **The student:** To Allah.
* **The Shaykh:** To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. To Him belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He leaves. And the decrees that occur, do they occur by chance, just like that? Answer.
* **The students:** No.
* **The Shaykh:** No. And everything with Him has a specified term; it does not come early or late.
  I will tell you two stories that I was told by someone I trust, which show what Allah's Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ indicate. A man told me, one of our imams, trustworthy, trustworthy, trustworthy, may Allah have mercy on him, he said: "We travelled to Hajj on camels. When we returned from Makkah, the mother of one of us became ill." He says: "So we stopped among the mountains in the ar-Ray'," do you know ar-Ray'?
* **The students:** Yes.
* **The Shaykh:** Between two mountains; that is, the course of a valley between two mountains. We stopped at the end of the night and slept, and when morning came we set out. This man busied himself with his mother, arranging the saddle for her, and the people went on. The two sides of the valley hide a person. When he had arranged the saddle for his mother, he mounted her on the camel and went leading her, and he made a mistake; he lost the way, because people in the valleys hide from one another. He lost the way and took a path that he thought was the path leading to his companions. He walked and walked until the sun rose, and he did not find his companions. Then he saw a small tent, and there were people living there, Bedouins, from exhaustion. He and his mother stopped, and he asked them about the way. They said: "The way is behind you, but rest a little, you and the woman who is with you." He says: "When I had placed her on the ground, Allah took her soul." Allahu Akbar! Who could imagine that this man comes from al-Qasim, and his mother dies only in these ravines?! But ﴿No soul knows in what land it will die.﴾ [Luqman 34].

  The second example: at one of the market intersections, there were two students who had left school three years before. There was a car wanting to cross. You know the way intersections work: each of them stopped. The two students at the door stopped, and the driver of the car stopped too. Each one wanted the other to cross first. In a second or two, the two students moved, and at the same time the car moved from the other side. The car struck the rear student, and he died immediately. Allahu Akbar!!

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 1, verse 1–7 (part 6 of 9):

It means seconds, so that this person remains until his term (ajal) comes to an end. So I say: ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Everything with Him has a term appointed"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari, no. 7377, and Muslim, no. 932/11), from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd.]]. Pay attention to the beneficial condolence (ta'ziyah) reported from the Messenger (ﷺ): how you say it when offering condolences to a person. You say: "Be patient and seek reward; for to Allah belongs what He takes and what He leaves, and everything with Him has a term appointed."

Now, there is a phrase common among people that the jurists (fuqaha', may Allah have mercy on them) have mentioned, they say: "May Allah magnify your reward, grant you good consolation, and forgive your deceased." This is good, but the words reported from the Messenger (ﷺ) are better, more beneficial, more protective, and more eloquent.

We say: condolence is in reality a form of worship, because in it there is kindness to the afflicted and strengthening him to bear the calamity. So do not add to it or subtract from it; do only what the Sharia has prescribed.

As for the third question:
* The student: After the iqamah...
* The Shaykh: Give me the third question before the questions run out.
* The student: He himself, may Allah establish it and make it endure.
* The Shaykh: Yes, does not the muezzin say: "And establish the prayer!"?
* The student: No.
* The Shaykh: As for people's saying at the iqamah of the prayer, "May Allah establish it and make it endure," this is based on a hadith reported on that subject, but it does not contain "as long as the heavens and the earth endure." Moreover, the hadith is weak. Therefore the correct position is that you do not respond to the one who gives the iqamah; you respond to the muezzin, and you do not respond to the one giving the iqamah, because the hadith reported on this is weak, and acts are not built upon weak hadiths. Just as some of the laypeople, when the imam says: ﴿Thee alone do we worship, and Thee alone do we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah 5], say: "We ask Allah for help." Do not say this; it is not reported. The Companions did not say it behind their Prophet. Moreover, the imam's recitation, you will say "amin" to it, so it is as if you yourself said: "Thee alone do we ask for help," and "Thee alone do we ask for help" is more eloquent than "We asked Allah for help."

Who knows rhetoric so that he can explain to us that it is more eloquent? "Thee alone do we ask for help" is more eloquent than "We asked Allah for help." Why?

It is more eloquent in two respects. First: in "iyyaka nasta'in" there is the fronting of the object (iyyaka), and the scholars said: fronting the object indicates what? It indicates restriction and exclusivity, as if you said: "We ask for help only from You."

The second respect: the phrase "asta'ana billah" is a past tense verb, but "nasta'in" is a present tense verb which indicates continuity, and the person is one who seeks help from Allah always and forever. Therefore there is no need to say "asta'ana billah." Listen to the recitation of your imam, and do not speak, for you are commanded to listen in silence, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said. When he says ﴿nor of those who are astray﴾, say: "Amin."

* The student: This questioner asks: Often some farmers sell wheat before delivering it to the silos, on the condition that its entry into the silos is in the name of the seller while the buyer pays its price, and thus the buyer pays the price of the wheat in advance to the seller?
* The Shaykh: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
This transaction is not permissible, because it is not allowed to deliver the wheat while its owner is in the name of another person, for this involves falling into falsehood. The wheat, after it has been sold to a certain person, is no longer the property of that other person. There is also in it a betrayal of the state, because it was entered into the silos in the name of a person while it belonged to someone else. And there is in it consuming wealth falsely, because the gain that the buyer obtains was obtained by a forbidden means, and every gain obtained by a forbidden means is consuming wealth falsely. The fourth of the corruptions is that when the people follow these crooked paths, they become an animal people, having no concern except worldly gain alone, not fearing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and not looking to the Hereafter, as if they were created for wealth. The truth is that wealth was created for us; we were not created for it. Whoever torments himself with wealth is tormented, and whoever makes wealth serve his interests, Allah makes his affair easy. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿He it is who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 29]; He did not say: "He created you for what is on the earth." Rather, Allah created us for His worship: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 56]. So I warn my Muslim brothers against such actions by which they gain wealth through forbidden means, because of the harm to them in their livelihood and their Hereafter.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner asks: What is the ruling on differentiating between the takbirs of the prayer, lengthening some and shortening others, with the aim of making the followers understand the action that follows the takbir?
* The Shaykh: The ruling on this has no basis in the Sunnah. It is not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he differentiated between the takbirs, and I do not know of any jurist who said so. The most I have come across in the statements of the jurists is that some of them said: one should lengthen the takbir in lowering from standing to prostration and in rising from prostration to standing, saying: because the interval between these two pillars is long, so the takbir is lengthened to cover the time of rising and the time of lowering. Yet they said this without proof from the Sunnah; they said it only by ijtihad. That is, you say, when you want to prostrate: "Allah is greatest," so that you begin the takbir as soon as you start to descend, and it ends upon reaching the ground. And when you rise from prostration, say "Allah is greatest," so that you begin the takbir from the prostration at the time of (...) the prostration, and it ends with the completion of standing, or upon reaching standing. But they said it only by ijtihad. Since this matter has come with the Sunnah, that is, the Messenger (ﷺ) used to say the takbir and it is not reported from him that he differentiated between the takbirs, the Sunnah is not to differentiate.

In not differentiating between the takbirs there is great benefit for the follower, because the follower lowers his attention and pays attention to the rak'ahs. But if he follows the imam according to his takbirs, he becomes like a mechanical machine, walking behind this takbir, and by Allah he does not know whether it is the first or the second. As for when the imam does not differentiate, you find the person giving his full attention, because he fears that he will stand in a place of sitting or sit in a place of standing before the people and be embarrassed. Therefore I saw benefit in it. At the beginning of my leading prayers I used to differentiate between the takbirs, following the custom of the people, but some of the brothers, may Allah reward them with good, who are attentive to hadith, alerted me and said: "My brother, what is your evidence for this? Bring me evidence, or do not do it." When he said this to me, in truth he overwhelmed me; I could not answer him on that. So I said: "May Allah reward you with good; God willing, I will not differentiate after this." When I prayed for the first time and did not differentiate, the followers glorified Allah with me, saying: "Subhan Allah!" because their custom was that we differentiate. But after two or three times this passed, and they understood that there is no differentiation, and each one began to take a thousand accounts so that he would not go and forget in his prayer and err before the people. It may be that this is supported by the fact that the Prophet did not differentiate between the takbirs: when a pulpit (minbar) was made for him, he (ﷺ) would stand on the pulpit, recite, and bow on the pulpit; when he wanted to prostrate, he came down from the pulpit and prostrated on the ground. Then he (ﷺ) said: "I only did that so that you may follow me and learn my prayer"[[A hadith agreed upon (Bukhari, no. 917, and Muslim, no. 544/44), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]]. As for his saying "so that you may learn my prayer," this is yes, whenever a person is raised and visible to the followers, they learn more. But "so that you may follow me"? This is evidence that he did not differentiate between the takbirs, otherwise following would be by differentiating between the takbirs. And Allah knows best.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: Some people set aside Friday for visiting graves. Is there a basis for this in the Sharia?
* The Shaykh: As for specifying Friday for visiting graves, I do not know of any basis for it in the Sharia. But some jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, said: visiting should be on Friday; and some of them also said: on Friday before sunrise. But since this view has no trace of evidence, it should not be acted upon as a rule; visiting graves is at any time. As I indicated earlier, before the prayer the Prophet (ﷺ) visited the graveyard at night, as in the long hadith of 'A'ishah[[Reported by Muslim, no. 974/103, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]].
* The student: Thank you, may Allah grant you thanks. This one says: We often hear about raising the hands in supplication after voluntary prayer and wiping the face after the supplication. What is the ruling on that, may Allah reward you?
* The Shaykh: As for wiping the face with the hands after supplication, whether after a voluntary prayer or in another place, there are hadiths reported about this, but all of their chains are weak, all of them weak. Some scholars said: the combination of these weak chains raises the hadith to the level of hasan (sound) li-ghayrihi (through another), which the people of hadith call hasan li-ghayrihi, meaning not in itself; and on this Ibn Hajar went, as in Bulugh al-Maram.

Other scholars said: these weak hadiths are not strengthened by the multiplicity of their chains, due to their severe weakness. Among those who held this view was Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said: wiping the face with the hands after supplication is not a Sunnah. Not wiping is more appropriate, because if it were a Sunnah it would be well known and famous. As for raising the hands in supplication, this also has no basis, neither after the obligatory prayer nor after the voluntary prayer. The most that is reported on it is that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which supplication is most heard?" He said: "In the last part of the night and after the prescribed prayers"[[Reported by al-Tirmidhi, no. 3499, and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 9856, from the hadith of Abu Umamah.]]. And the word "adbar": does it mean its end, or what follows it?

Some scholars say: "adbar al-salawat" means what follows them, and others say it means their end. Nevertheless, it is not reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he raised his hands in supplication, neither after the obligatory prayer nor after the voluntary prayer. Had it been good, the Prophet (ﷺ) would have explained it to his community, either by his words or by his deeds, or Allah would have facilitated for someone among the Companions in his time to do it, or in his presence, until its legislation is established. But what appears to me preponderant is that if what is tied to "adbar" is remembrance (dhikr), then it is after the prayer; and if what is tied to "adbar" is supplication (du'a'), then it is before the salam. The evidence: remembrance was commanded by Allah after the prayer, He said: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah﴾ [an-Nisa' 103]; and supplication was commanded by the Prophet (ﷺ) before the salam, in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, when he mentioned the tashahhud, he said: "Then let him choose from supplication whatever he wishes"[[Agreed upon (Bukhari, no. 835, and Muslim, no. 402/55), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with the wording: "Then let him choose from supplication what is most pleasing to him and supplicate with it."]].

On this basis we say: what is reported of supplication restricted to "adbar al-salawat" we take to mean before the salam, because that is the place of supplication; and what is reported of remembrance restricted to "adbar al-salawat" we take to mean after the salam, because that is what Allah commanded in His words: ﴿So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ [an-Nisa' 103]; and because the meaning requires that supplication be before the salam, since before a person gives the salam he is still before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When he turns away from his prayer, he turns away. So which is better: to confide in your Lord in supplication while you are confiding in Him in your prayer, or after you have turned away?
* The student: In the prayer is better.
* The Shaykh: In the prayer is better, yes.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: We heard that your eminence has authenticated the completion of the supplication after the adhan: "Innaka la tukhlifu al-mi'ad" [[Reported by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 1933, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]]. Is that correct?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is correct. I authenticated it, and so did others. I do not mean that I authenticated it myself; rather it was authenticated by others among the people of knowledge who are more knowledgeable than us in hadith. Whoever said it is weak was refuted in my presence and could not answer the refutation, because the one who said it is weak was confused by one of the narrators: there is a narrator whose name is shared by two men, one of them weak and the other trustworthy, and the one who weakened it thought the name refers to the weak man, so he weakened it for that reason. Those who authenticated it said: this man you imagined is not the one intended in the context, and therefore this wording is the authentic one.
* The student: May Allah reward you. This questioner says: A man sold his palm trees to another man, and each of them assumed the other had paid zakat on the fruit; after a year it became clear that neither had paid it. Is the zakat upon the seller or the buyer? And may he give money in place of the fruit?
* The Shaykh: The zakat is upon the seller; that is, if fruits are sold and they are of the kind subject to zakat, the zakat is upon the seller, because the goodness (salah) has appeared in his property, and when the ripening of the fruit appears, zakat becomes due on it. Based on this, our answer to this question is: the seller must pay zakat on it; he pays zakat on the fruit of his palms that he sold. And how does he pay it? He gives out half of its tenth if it is irrigated with buckets (makayil) or with water-wheels (sawani); I think the water-wheels do not exist here.
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Then by buckets: he gives out half the tenth. How much is half of a tenth in relation to a hundred? O calculators, how much is half a tenth in relation to a hundred?
* A student: A quarter of a tenth.
* The Shaykh: No, sir, a quarter of a tenth; five percent. A quarter of a tenth in relation to a hundred is five percent. And if it is irrigated by flowing water or by rain from the (...) or otherwise?
* A student: Its tenth.
* The Shaykh: How much is due? The tenth. How much is a tenth in relation to a hundred?
* A student: Ten.
